ekadashi.name: Utpanna Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Destroys sins accumulated over millions of lives and grants liberation.
ekadashi.story: The appearance day of Ekadashi Devi from Lord Vishnu's body to destroy the demon Mura.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, 4 December 2026

The glory of Utpanna Ekadashi is described in the Bhavishyottara Purana in a conversation between Sri Krishna and Arjuna.

Sri Suta Goswami told the assembled brahmanas and sages: "One who hears with faith and devotion about the glory of Ekadashi and the rules given by Lord Krishna attains happiness in this life and, in the next life, reaches the abode of Lord Vishnu."

Arjuna once asked Sri Krishna: "O Janardana, please explain the merit of fasting completely, eating only in the evening, or taking food once at midday on Ekadashi."

Lord Sri Krishna replied: "O Arjuna, at the beginning of autumn, on the Ekadashi that falls during the waning moon in November-December, one should begin the observance of Ekadashi. Early in the morning one should take a vow to fast. At midday one should purify oneself by bathing, praying to Mother Earth to remove the reactions of sinful actions and to grant the path to the supreme abode. After bathing, one should worship Lord Govinda."

The Lord then described how Indra, surrounded by the devas, once approached the Supreme Lord in distress. The devas had been driven from heaven by the powerful demon Mura. Indra prayed: "O Lord of the universe, O Supreme Personality of Godhead, You are the shelter, mother, and father of all. You create, maintain, and withdraw everything. We have lost our heavenly kingdom and have fallen into suffering. Please be pleased with us."

Hearing this plea, Lord Vishnu asked Indra to explain who had conquered the devas. Indra answered that the fierce demon Mura, son of Nadijangha, had taken the heavenly kingdom and assumed the positions of the devas. Even when united, the devas could not defeat him.

Lord Vishnu became angry on behalf of the devas and went with them to Mura's capital, Chandravati. A terrible battle began. Although the Lord easily defeated the demonic armies, Mura himself could not be subdued by any weapon. The struggle continued for a very long time, and at last the Lord went to Badarikashram and entered a beautiful cave named Hemavati to rest.

Mura followed Him into the cave and, seeing the Lord apparently asleep, prepared to attack Him. At that moment a radiant goddess appeared from the Lord's own body, armed with divine weapons. She fought with Mura and cut off his head, causing his followers to flee in fear.

When the Lord awoke, He saw Mura lying dead and the effulgent goddess standing before Him with folded palms. He asked who she was. She replied: "O my Lord, I appeared from Your body and killed this demon. Seeing You asleep, he tried to attack You, and I stopped him."

The Supreme Lord said: "O Goddess, I am pleased with you and grateful to you. Ask any boon. You are My spiritual energy. Because you appeared on the day of Ekadashi, your name shall be Ekadashi. Whoever observes the vow of Ekadashi will be freed from the reactions of sinful actions and will attain divine happiness."

From that time onward, Ekadashi has been honored in this world. The Lord told Arjuna that one who follows the Ekadashi vow is awarded the highest destination. He also explained that Ekadashi joined with Dvadashi is especially auspicious, and that on Ekadashi one should avoid sense indulgence, grains and beans, honey, meat, inappropriate vessels, and the use of oil.

Thus ends the account of the glory of Utpanna Ekadashi.

ekadashi.name: Mokshada Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Grants liberation from the material world and washes away bad karma.
ekadashi.story: On this day Lord Krishna spoke the Bhagavad-gita to Arjuna on the field of Kurukshetra.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, 20 December 2026

Mokshada Ekadashi falls during the waxing moon in November-December. Its glory is described in the Brahmanda Purana in a conversation between Lord Krishna and Maharaja Yudhishthira.

Yudhishthira once asked Lord Krishna: "My dear Krishna, what is the name of the Ekadashi that comes during the waxing moon in November-December? Please also describe the proper observance of this Ekadashi."

Lord Krishna replied: "O best of kings, this Ekadashi destroys the reactions of sinful actions. If on this day one worships the Supreme Lord with tulasi manjaris, the Lord becomes very pleased. By observing this Ekadashi one receives the result of performing a Vajapeya sacrifice."

In ancient times there was a king named Vaikhanasa who ruled the city of Champaka. He was kind to his subjects, and many learned brahmanas lived in his kingdom. One night the king dreamed that his father had fallen into hell and was suffering terribly. Deeply disturbed, the king told the brahmanas about the dream the next day.

In the dream, his father begged to be delivered from hell. From that time the king lost all peace. He found no taste in royal power, wealth, family life, or state affairs. He thought that all his prosperity was useless if his father was suffering. In distress he asked the learned brahmanas: "Please tell me how I can rescue my father from hell."

The brahmanas replied: "O king, the ashram of Parvata Muni is nearby. He knows past, present, and future. Go to him and explain your dream." Following their advice, King Vaikhanasa went to the sage with the brahmanas and his subjects.

When Parvata Muni asked about the welfare of the kingdom, the king answered: "By your mercy we are all well, but I am suffering greatly. Although I have a kingdom and every kind of wealth, doubts and pain fill my mind." He then described the dream.

Parvata Muni entered meditation. After some time he said: "My dear king, in a previous life your father was overcome by lust, and for that reason he is now suffering in hell. You should observe the Ekadashi vow during the waxing moon in November-December and offer the merit of that observance to your father. By the power of your piety he will be delivered."

Hearing the sage's instruction, the king returned to his palace. When the proper day arrived, the king, his wife, his children, and his servants observed that Ekadashi with care. The merit produced by the vow was offered to the king's father, who was then delivered and attained the heavenly realm, blessing his son.

Lord Krishna concluded: "O king, one who properly observes Mokshada Ekadashi becomes free from the reactions of past sins." This Ekadashi is also remembered as the sacred day on which Lord Krishna spoke the Bhagavad-gita to Arjuna at Kurukshetra, opening the path of liberation for all souls.

ekadashi.name: Сапхала экадаши
ekadashi.benefits: Дарует успех во всех начинаниях и духовное процветание.
ekadashi.story: Помогает искупить даже самые тяжкие грехи благодаря искреннему раскаянию.

ekadashi.name: Путрада экадаши
ekadashi.benefits: Благословляет праведным и благочестивым потомством, приносит мир в семью.
ekadashi.story: Связан с историей царя Сукетумана, которому пост помог избавиться от горя.

ekadashi.name: Shat-tila Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Purifies sins, grants health, and relieves bodily suffering.
ekadashi.story: Connected with charity and the six traditional uses of sesame seeds.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, January 14, 2026

This Ekadashi falls during the waning moon in the month of January/February. The glories of Shat-tila Ekadashi are described in the Bhavishya Uttara Purana.

Once, the sage Dalbhya asked the sage Pulastya: “O respected brahmana, people commit various sinful acts—they kill brahmanas and indulge their senses in this temporary world. Please explain to me how they can be freed from the hellish condition into which they fall as a result of their sins.”

The sage Pulastya replied: “O most fortunate one! On the Ekadashi that falls during the waning moon in the month of January/February, one should worship the Supreme Lord. While performing worship, one should pray as follows: ‘O Lord Janardana! O most merciful Lord Krishna, You are the savior of sinners. Please be merciful to those who have sunk into the ocean of material existence. O Supreme Brahman! O Supreme Personality of Godhead! O Lord of the universe! Please accept my worship, and may Your consort Lakshmidevi also accept it.’

After worshiping the Lord, one should worship the brahmanas by giving them canopies, clothing, footwear, and vessels filled with water. According to one’s means, one should also offer a black cow and sesame seeds to the best of the brahmanas. By giving sesame seeds in charity, one obtains the opportunity to live in heaven for many years.

On this Ekadashi, one should bathe in water mixed with sesame seeds, apply sesame paste to the body, perform a fire sacrifice with sesame seeds, offer the forefathers water mixed with sesame seeds, eat sesame seeds, and freely distribute sesame seeds in charity. By these acts, all the reactions to sinful activities are destroyed. Therefore, this Ekadashi is called Shat-tila Ekadashi.

When Narada Muni desired to hear from Krishna about the glories of Shat-tila Ekadashi and the results of observing it, Lord Krishna told the Muni the following story.

“In ancient times there lived a brahmani woman. She strictly observed the Ekadashi vow and worshiped the Lord. By constantly following various vows in the course of her worship, she became weak and thin. Although she gave gifts to poor brahmanas and unmarried girls, she never satisfied the brahmanas and demigods by offering them grains. Therefore, I consider that although the brahmani’s body became weakened because she performed severe austerities, she was a pure soul. Yet she never gave grains to the hungry.

O best of brahmanas! Desiring to test this brahmani, I assumed the form of a beggar and appeared in this temporary world. Holding a begging bowl in My hand, I came to the woman’s house. She said, ‘O brahmana! Please tell me where you have come from.’ I pretended not to hear her and again begged for alms. The woman became angry, took a handful of clay, and placed it in My begging bowl. After that, I returned to My abode.

By virtue of her austerities, the brahmani woman also returned to My abode. Although she had a beautiful house, because she had offered Me a lump of clay, there was neither wealth nor grain in that house. O brahmana! When she entered the house, she found nothing there. Because she had no wealth, the woman lost her peace of mind. She approached Me and angrily said, ‘O Janardana! I performed severe austerities, observed vows, and worshiped Lord Vishnu. Why, then, am I deprived of grain and wealth?’ I replied to the woman, ‘O brahmani! You have come here from the material world. Now, please return home. When the wives of the demigods, moved by curiosity, come to your house to have your darshan, you should ask them about the glories of Shat-tila Ekadashi. Do not open the door until they have completed the narration.’ Having heard Me, the brahmani returned home.

One day, while the brahmani was sitting in her room with the door locked from within, the wives of the demigods arrived. They said, ‘O beautiful one! We have come here to have your darshan. Please open the door.’ The brahmani replied, ‘If you wish to see me, then before I open the door, please tell me about the significance and glories of Shat-tila Ekadashi and the merit gained by observing it.’ Then one of the wives of the demigods narrated the glories of this Ekadashi. Hearing the narration, the brahmani was satisfied and opened the door for them. Upon seeing the brahmani, the wives of the demigods rejoiced. Following the instructions of these goddesses, the brahmani observed the vow of Shat-tila Ekadashi. By doing so, she became beautiful and radiant, and possessed sufficient grain, wealth, and gold.

However, no one should observe this Ekadashi out of greed. By following this Ekadashi, misfortune and poverty disappear. If one gives sesame seeds in charity on this day, all the reactions to one’s sinful activities are destroyed.”

ekadashi.name: Jaya Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Frees one from lower conditions and from fear of ghosts or spirits.
ekadashi.story: Fasting on this day elevates consciousness and grants the mercy of Lord Vishnu.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, January 29, 2026

The glories of Jaya (Bhaimi) Ekadashi, which falls during the waxing moon in the month of January/February, are described in the Bhavishya Uttara Purana in a conversation between Lord Krishna and Maharaja Yudhishthira.

Once Maharaja Yudhishthira asked Lord Krishna: “O Lord Krishna! O original Personality of Godhead, O Lord of the universe, Sri Krishna! You are the original source of the four categories of living beings—those born from perspiration, those born from seeds, those born from eggs, and those born from embryos. You alone create, maintain, and destroy everything that exists. Please describe to me the glories of the Ekadashi that falls during the waxing moon in the month of January/February. Please also describe the practice of observing this Ekadashi and tell me which deity should be worshiped on this auspicious day.”

Lord Krishna said: “O best of kings, Yudhishthira! The Ekadashi that falls during the waxing moon in the month of January/February is celebrated as Jaya Ekadashi. Observing this Ekadashi removes all reactions to sinful activities. One who observes this Ekadashi is never born as a ghost. O king! This Ekadashi has no equal in its power to grant liberation and remove the reactions to sinful activities. O lion-like king! Now please hear the description of this Ekadashi, which I have already related in the Padma Purana.

The fortunate demigods lived in the heavenly kingdom of Indra. In the Nandana Kanana forest, filled with the fragrance of blooming Parijata flowers, where the apsaras sported, Indra enjoyed their company. One day, being in a cheerful mood, Indra arranged a festival in which fifty million apsaras participated. Present at that assembly was a Gandharva singer named Pushpadanta. Another Gandharva named Chitrasena came to the assembly with his wife Malini and his daughter. Chitrasena had a son named Pushpavana, and Pushpavana’s son was named Malyavan. A Gandharvi named Pushpavati was captivated by Malyavan’s beauty, pierced by the sharp arrows of Cupid. Beautiful Pushpavati tried in every way, by gestures and glances, to bring Malyavan under her control.

O king! How can I describe to you the astonishing beauty of Pushpavati? Her beautiful arms resembled the ropes of Cupid, and the beauty of her face resembled the beauty of the moon. Her eyes were wide, her ears adorned with earrings, her waist slender, her breasts full, and her hips broad, resembling the trunk of a banana tree. Her radiant feet surpassed the beauty of red lotuses. Her graceful limbs appeared even more enchanting because they were adorned with splendid ornaments and garments. Malyavan was conquered by Pushpavati. Desiring to please Indra, Malyavan and Pushpavati began to sing and dance together with the other apsaras. But because they were mutually attracted, they could not dance flawlessly. Both were pierced by Cupid’s arrows.

Indra, noticing that the singing and dancing had been disrupted, understood what the lovers were feeling. Because they had caused a disturbance, Indra felt insulted and declared: ‘You are foolish and sinful. You have disobeyed me; therefore I curse you. You shall become male and female ghosts and be born on earth, where you will suffer the consequences of your karma.’

Thus cursed, Malyavan and Pushpavati obtained ghostly bodies and began to live a miserable life in a cave in the Himalayan mountains. Because they were in the bodies of ghosts, they felt despair and grief. Under the influence of the curse, they could not enjoy fragrance, touch, or sleep. One day, while wandering through the dense forests and cold mountains of the Himalayas, they sat down in one place and began to reflect. The male ghost said to the female ghost: ‘Alas, what terrible deeds have we committed that we are now trapped in these miserable ghostly bodies?’

Malyavan and Pushpavati passed their days and nights without food or drink, repenting their sins. One day the auspicious occasion of Jaya Ekadashi arrived, observed during the waxing moon in the month of January/February. Although the ghosts suffered unbearably from hunger and thirst, they naturally could not kill anyone. Likewise, they could not eat roots or fruits, nor could they drink. O king! Thus, when the ghostly couple sat beneath a banyan tree, the sun began to set. Because of the cold and their sorrowful thoughts, they passed the entire night without sleep. As their minds were disturbed, no desire for sense enjoyment arose in their hearts. O lion-hearted king! Thus, without even knowing it, they observed the vow of Jaya Ekadashi, and by the influence of the merit gained thereby, on the very next day they became free from their ghostly bodies.

After that, Pushpavati and Malyavan returned to heaven in an aerial vehicle. There they approached Indra, the king of the demigods, and offered him their obeisances. Seeing them, Indra was astonished and said: ‘What wonder is this! By what merit have you ceased to be ghosts? Which demigod has freed you from my curse?’ Malyavan replied: ‘By the causeless mercy of the Supreme Lord and as a result of observing the vow of Jaya Ekadashi, we have been freed from the curse. O lord! I declare to you with full conviction that we were delivered from our ghostly forms simply by devotional service.’

Hearing these words, Indra said to Malyavan: ‘You have become purified by rendering devotional service to Lord Vishnu and observing the Ekadashi vow. Therefore, you are now worthy of my worship as well. Those who render devotional service to Vishnu are undoubtedly objects of my worship and reverence.’ Pushpavati and Malyavan then lived happily in heaven.

O King Yudhishthira! One should observe this Ekadashi. Following the vow of Jaya Ekadashi frees one even from the sin of killing a brahmana. Moreover, by observing this vow, one automatically gains the merit arising from charity, sacrifices, and pilgrimages. If a person properly observes this Ekadashi with faith and devotion, he becomes an eternal resident of Vaikuntha. Simply by reading or hearing about the glories of this Ekadashi, one obtains the results of performing the Agnishtoma sacrifice.”

ekadashi.name: Vijaya Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Grants victory over enemies, helps overcome obstacles, and brings success.
ekadashi.story: Lord Ramachandra observed this fast before marching to Lanka to defeat Ravana.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, February 13, 2026

The glories of this Ekadashi are described in the Skanda Purana. Once Maharaja Yudhishthira addressed Lord Krishna: “O Lord Krishna, please be kind to me and describe the Ekadashi that falls during the waning moon in the month of February/March.”

Lord Krishna replied: “O King Yudhishthira! I shall gladly tell you about the Ekadashi known as Vijaya Ekadashi. By observing this Ekadashi, the reactions to sinful activities are immediately destroyed.

Once the great sage Narada approached Lord Brahma: ‘O best of the demigods! Please tell me about the fruits attained by observing the vow of Vijaya Ekadashi, which falls during the waning moon in the month of February/March.’ Lord Brahma replied: ‘My dear son, this ancient vow is pure and destroys the consequences of all sins. Its fruits are great, as indicated by the very name of this Ekadashi. Without doubt, Vijaya Ekadashi empowers a person to attain victory.

When Sri Ramachandra, His consort Sitadevi, and His brother Lakshmana went into exile for fourteen years by the order of Ramachandra’s father, they lived for some time in the beautiful forest known as Panchavati, situated on the bank of the Godavari River. The austere Sitadevi was abducted by Ravana, the king of the demons. Separation from Sita plunged Ramachandra into an ocean of sorrow.

While wandering through the forest in search of Sita, Ramachandra encountered Jatayu, the king of birds, who was near death. Jatayu told Ramachandra everything he knew about Sita and then departed from this world and returned to Vaikuntha. Later Ramachandra formed a friendship with Sugriva. Desiring to assist Ramachandra’s mission, numerous monkey soldiers assembled into an army. At that time Hanuman, the king of the monkeys, reached the Ashoka grove in Lanka, where he met Sitadevi and gave her Ramachandra’s ring. Then Hanuman returned to Ramachandra and brought him the news.

After hearing Hanuman’s account, Ramachandra met with His friend Sugriva and resolved to invade Lanka. Ramachandra assembled a vast number of monkey soldiers and reached the shore of the ocean. He asked Lakshmana: ‘O Saumitra! How shall we cross this bottomless ocean, teeming with whales and crocodiles?’ Lakshmana replied: ‘O original Supreme Personality of Godhead! You are the original Lord. On this island lives a great sage named Bakadalbhya. His ashrama is four miles from here. O son of the Raghu dynasty! This sage has had the darshan of Lord Brahma. We should ask him how the ocean may be crossed.’

Thus, following Lakshmana’s advice, Lord Ramachandra went to the ashrama of Bakadalbhya and offered him respectful obeisances. The omniscient sage immediately understood that the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Ramachandra, stood before him. He had appeared in this material world to kill the demon Ravana. The great sage asked: ‘O Ramachandra, for what purpose have You come here?’ Ramachandra replied: ‘O brahmana! By your mercy I have come here to the shore of the ocean with My soldiers. I desire to fight the demons and conquer Lanka. O best of sages! Please tell Me a simple means by which I can cross the ocean. Only for this reason have I come to your lotus feet.’ The great sage said to Ramachandra: ‘O Ramachandra! I shall tell You about the observance of a great vow by which You will be able to win the battle and obtain fame and prosperity in this world. You must follow this vow with the utmost attention. O Rama! There is an Ekadashi known as Vijaya, which falls in the month of February/March. By observing this Ekadashi, You will be able to cross the ocean together with Your monkey soldiers. O Lord Ramachandra! Now please hear the procedure for observing this Ekadashi.

On the day before Ekadashi, You should fill a golden, silver, copper, or earthen vessel with water and decorate it with mango shoots. Then this vessel should be placed upon a sanctified elevated altar adorned with seven kinds of grain. After that, a golden deity of Lord Narayana should be placed upon the vessel. On Ekadashi day, You should bathe early in the morning and worship the deity of Lord Narayana with devotion, offering tulasi leaves, sandalwood paste, flowers, garlands, incense, a ghee lamp, and food. At night You should remain awake. On the day after Ekadashi, after sunrise, You should place the vessel on the bank of a river, pond, or lake and properly worship it. Then You should give the vessel and the deity of Narayana in charity to a brahmana who strictly observes the vow of celibacy. By doing all that has been described above, You will certainly prevail over Your enemies.’

Following the instructions of this great sage, Lord Ramachandra demonstrated the ideal example of observing this Ekadashi vow and won the battle. A person who properly observes this Ekadashi vow will certainly become victorious both in this life and in the next.

Lord Brahma continued, addressing Narada: ‘O my dear son! Therefore, everyone should observe the vow of this Vijaya Ekadashi. The glories of Vijaya Ekadashi destroy all reactions to sinful activities. A person who reads or hears the glories of this Ekadashi obtains the results of the Vajapeya sacrifice.’”

ekadashi.name: Amalaki Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Purifies sins, is praised like a sacrifice, and grants spiritual knowledge.
ekadashi.story: Connected with worship of the amla tree as a manifestation of Krishna’s energy.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, February 27, 2026

The glories of Amalaki Ekadashi, which falls during the waxing moon in the month of February/March, are described in the Brahmanda Purana in a conversation between King Mandhata and the sage Vasishtha.

Once King Mandhata addressed the sage Vasishtha: “O most fortunate one, if you are pleased with me and merciful toward me, then please tell me of a vow by following which I may attain all auspiciousness.”

The sage Vasishtha replied: “O king! Now I shall tell you the glories and history of a great vow, the observance of which bestows complete auspiciousness upon a person. O king! This vow is known as Amalaki Vrata Ekadashi. The influence of the merit acquired by observing this Ekadashi certainly destroys the consequences of all sinful activities, grants liberation, and gives the result of giving one thousand cows in charity.

In ancient times there was a city called Vaidisha. Many healthy and prosperous brahmanas, kshatriyas, vaishyas, and shudras lived there. O lion-hearted king, in that beautiful city there were neither atheists nor sinners. The city was filled with the sound of Vedic mantras. In this glorious city lived a truthful and pious king named Chaitraratha, born in the family of King Pashabinduka of the lunar dynasty.

King Chaitraratha was valiant, courageous, generous, and learned in the scriptures. Because all the inhabitants of the kingdom rendered devotional service to Lord Hari, they all lived happily. There was not a single poor or suffering person in the entire kingdom. Many years passed in this way, and one day Amalaki Ekadashi coincided with Dvadashi during the waning moon in the month of February/March.

Understanding that this Ekadashi brings great benefits, the king and his subjects decided to observe it according to all rules and regulations. Early in the morning on Ekadashi day, the king and his subjects bathed in the river and went to the temple of Lord Vishnu situated on its bank. In the temple there was an amalaki tree, where the king placed a vessel of water, along with an umbrella, clothing, footwear, and five kinds of jewels for worship. Then the king worshiped Lord Parashurama and the amalaki tree, offering water, footwear, an umbrella, gold, diamonds, rubies, pearls, sapphires, and incense.

Then the king, led by sages and accompanied by his subjects, offered the following prayers to Lord Parashurama: ‘O Lord Parashurama! O son of Renuka! O You who dwell beneath the shade of the amalaki tree! O bestower of material enjoyment and liberation! I offer You my respectful obeisances.’ Then they offered prayers to the amalaki tree: ‘O amalaki! O tree that sustains the universe! O creation of Lord Brahma! O destroyer of sins! We offer you our respectful obeisances! Kindly accept our offerings.’

After properly worshiping the Lord and the amalaki tree, the king and his subjects remained awake throughout the night in the temple of Lord Vishnu. They sang songs and offered beautiful prayers glorifying the Lord and the amalaki tree. At that time, by the arrangement of providence, a certain hunter came to that place. This hunter maintained himself by killing various living beings. He entered the temple, which was decorated with ghee lamps, incense, and other auspicious articles, and saw a group of people remaining awake and glorifying the Lord. He sat near them and watched.

The fortunate hunter had the darshan of Lord Damodara situated atop a special vessel and heard transcendental narrations about Vishnu. Although tormented by hunger, the hunter watched everything with astonishment and remained awake the entire night, hearing the glories of Ekadashi.

In the morning, the king left the temple and returned to the palace with his retinue. The hunter also returned home and, being satisfied, ate. Years later, the hunter left his body. By the influence of Amalaki Ekadashi and because he had remained awake on the night of Ekadashi, in his next life the hunter became a king, possessing innumerable elephants, horses, chariots, and a great army. The hunter was born as Vasuratha, the mighty son of King Viduratha, ruler of the famous city of Jayanti.

King Vasuratha was the lord of one million villages. He was dazzling like the sun, radiant like the moon, powerful like Lord Vishnu, and patient like Mother Earth. The king was truthful, steadfast in performing his prescribed duty, and a great devotee of Lord Vishnu.

One day, the kind and generous King Vasuratha became lost in the forest while hunting. He was exhausted and hungry. Seeing no way out, the king lay down on the ground in the dense forest, using his arm as a pillow. At that time, certain mlecchas who lived in that forest approached the king and began to torment him in various ways. Considering the king their enemy, they tried to kill him. The mlecchas thought that in the past the king had killed their mothers, sons, and grandsons and had forced them to live a miserable life in the forest. Making such accusations, the mlecchas took up their weapons and began to strike the king. Yet, to their great astonishment, their weapons could not even touch the king’s body, and therefore he did not feel the slightest pain. Having tried every means, the mlecchas became sorrowful and afraid. They were unable to move from the spot.

At that time, a beautiful woman emerged from the king’s body, richly adorned and anointed with fragrant sandalwood paste. She was decorated with an exquisite flower garland, and her eyes were red with anger. Holding a disc in her hand and raising her eyebrows, she furiously attacked the mlecchas, intent on killing them. Within a moment all the mlecchas were dead. Then the king regained consciousness. Seeing this terrifying scene, the king became frightened and bewildered. Seeing that his formidable enemies had been slain, he was astonished and said: ‘Alas! Who is the well-wisher and friend who saved my life by killing my powerful enemies? I am sincerely grateful to him for this kindness.’ Then a celestial voice was heard: ‘Who but Lord Keshava can protect a soul devoted to Him? He is the sole protector of His devotees.’ Hearing the celestial voice, the king became still more astonished, and his heart overflowed with devotional feelings.

After that, the king returned to the palace and ruled his kingdom like Indra, without encountering any obstacles.”

The sage Vasishtha continued: “My dear king! Anyone who observes the vow of this sacred Amalaki Ekadashi will certainly return to the abode of Lord Vishnu.”

ekadashi.name: Papamochani Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Destroys the reactions of even very grave sins committed in ignorance.
ekadashi.story: Grants forgiveness and helps restore spiritual purity after falldowns.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, March 15, 2026

The glories of Papamochani Ekadashi are described in the Bhavishyottara Purana in a conversation between Lord Krishna and Maharaja Yudhishthira.

Once Maharaja Yudhishthira addressed Lord Krishna: “My dear Lord Krishna, You have already told me the glories of Amalaki Ekadashi; now, please tell me about the Ekadashi that occurs during the waning moon in the month of March/April. What is the name of this Ekadashi? What is the process of observing it, and what are its results?”

Lord Krishna replied: “O best of kings! The name of this Ekadashi is Papamochani. Now please hear of its glories. Long ago, the sage Lomasa narrated the glories of this Ekadashi to King Mandhata.

This Papamochani Ekadashi falls during the waning moon in the month of March/April. This Ekadashi nullifies all reactions to sinful activities and bestows the eight kinds of mystic perfection.

The sage Lomasa said: ‘In ancient times, Kubera, the treasurer of the demigods, possessed a beautiful flower-filled forest known as Chaitraratha, where the weather was so pleasant that it seemed eternal spring prevailed.

In that forest Gandharvas and Kinnaras sported. The demigods, led by Indra, often came to the forest and pleasantly spent their time there. A great sage named Medhavi, a devotee of Lord Shiva, performed austerities in that forest.

The apsaras—the celestial dancing girls—tried in every way to disturb the sage. Among them was a celebrated apsara named Manju Ghosha. She sought a means to attract the sage’s attention.

Fearing the sage, Manju Ghosha built a hut near his ashrama and began singing in her sweet voice while accompanying herself on the vina. Seeing Manju Ghosha, who was anointed with sandalwood paste, adorned with a fragrant flower garland, sweetly singing, and extraordinarily attractive, Cupid, the enemy of Lord Shiva, sought to conquer the sage who worshiped Lord Shiva.

Because Lord Shiva had burned Cupid to ashes, Cupid, desiring revenge upon his destroyer, entered the body of the sage.

At that time the sage Medhavi, wearing a white sacred thread upon his body and dwelling in the ashrama of Chyavana Rishi, resembled a second Cupid. Inflamed with lust, Manju Ghosha slowly approached the sage.

The sage Medhavi also lost his reason because of lust and forgot the Lord whom he worshiped. He abandoned the practice of devotional service and became so intoxicated by the company of the beautiful woman that he lost the ability to distinguish day from night. Thus the sage spent many years in the company of the apsara.

When Manju Ghosha finally became convinced that the sage had lost his position, she decided to return to heaven. To Medhavi, who was absorbed in amorous enjoyment, she said: “O great sage! Now please give me permission to return home.”

The sage replied: “O beautiful woman! You came to me only to stay for the night, but when morning comes you may return.”

Hearing these words, Manju Ghosha became afraid and continued living in the sage’s company. Thus, although Manju Ghosha lived with the sage for fifty-seven years, nine months, and three days, to the sage it seemed that only half the night had passed.

Then Manju Ghosha again asked the sage for permission to return home, but the sage said: “O beautiful one! Please listen to me. It is only morning now. Please wait until I finish performing my morning rituals.” Astonished, the apsara smiled and said to the sage: “O great sage! How much time will you need to perform these rituals? Have you still not completed them? You have spent long years enjoying my company. Please consider how precious time is.”

Hearing such words from the apsara, the sage came to his senses and, calculating how much time had passed, said: “Alas! O beautiful one! I have wasted fifty-seven precious years of my life. You have caused the ruin of all my ascetic efforts.”

The sage’s eyes filled with tears, and his whole body trembled. The sage Medhavi cursed Manju Ghosha with these words: “You have behaved toward me like a witch; therefore you shall now become a witch. O sinful woman! Be cursed.”

Being cursed by the sage, Manju Ghosha humbly said to him: “O best of brahmanas! Please revoke the curse. I spent many years in your company. O my lord, you should forgive me.”

The sage replied: “O graceful one! What can I do now? You have destroyed all the wealth of my austerities. Nevertheless, I shall tell you of a practice by which you can become free from this curse. The Ekadashi that falls during the waning moon in the month of March/April, known as Papamochani, can destroy the consequences of all sinful activities. If you faithfully observe this Ekadashi, your suffering will come to an end.”

Having said this, the sage Medhavi returned to the ashrama of his spiritual father, the sage Chyavana. Seeing his fallen son, the sage Chyavana became sorrowful and said: “Alas! Alas! O my son, what have you done? You should not have destroyed all the wealth of your austerities by becoming the victim of an ordinary woman.”

The sage Medhavi replied: “O respected father! I am so unfortunate that I committed great sins in the company of an apsara. Therefore, please instruct me and tell me how I can atone for my sins.”

Hearing the plaintive words of his repentant son, the sage Chyavana said: “O my son! By observing Papamochani Ekadashi, which falls during the waning moon in the month of March/April, all reactions to sinful activities are completely destroyed.

Therefore you should observe this Ekadashi.” Having heard these compassionate words from his spiritual father, Medhavi observed this Ekadashi with special enthusiasm.

By the influence of this Ekadashi, all the reactions to his sinful activities were destroyed, and the sage Medhavi became extraordinarily virtuous.

At the same time, the beautiful Manju Ghosha also observed this auspicious Papamochani Ekadashi, and by doing so returned to heaven.’

After narrating this story to King Mandhata, the sage Lomasa concluded: ‘My dear king, by observing this Ekadashi, all reactions to sinful activities are automatically destroyed. By hearing or reading the glories of this Ekadashi, one attains the results of giving a thousand cows in charity. By observing this Ekadashi, all kinds of sins, such as killing a brahmana, killing an embryo, drinking intoxicants, and committing adultery with the wife of one’s guru, are completely neutralized. Because this sacred Ekadashi is so auspicious and destroys all sins, everyone should observe it.’”

ekadashi.name: Kamada Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Fulfills desires, frees one from curses, and grants liberation.
ekadashi.story: Purifies the mind and helps break the chains of material attachment.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, March 29, 2026

The glories of Kamada Ekadashi are described in the Varaha Purana in a conversation between Lord Krishna and Maharaja Yudhishthira.

Once Maharaja Yudhishthira addressed Lord Krishna, the crown jewel of the Yadu dynasty: “O Lord Vasudeva! Please accept my humble obeisances. Please tell me about the Ekadashi that falls during the waxing moon in the month of March/April. Also reveal to me the process of observing this Ekadashi and the benefits it bestows.”

Lord Krishna replied: “My dear Maharaja Yudhishthira, please attentively hear the description of this Ekadashi from the Puranas.

Once Maharaja Dilipa, the great-grandfather of Lord Ramachandra, asked his spiritual master, the sage Vasishtha, about the name and the process of observing the Ekadashi that falls during the waxing moon in the month of March/April.

The sage Vasishtha replied: ‘O king! I shall certainly fulfill your desire. The name of this Ekadashi is Kamada. This sacred Ekadashi burns all reactions to sinful activities to ashes and bestows upon its observer the blessing of obtaining a son.

Long ago there was a city called Ratnapura, also known as Bhogipura. This magnificent city was ruled by a king named Pundarika. Among his subjects were Gandharvas, Kinnaras, and apsaras. In this city lived a beautiful apsara named Lalita and an attractive Gandharva named Lalit. They were husband and wife. Their mutual love was all-consuming, and they constantly spent their time in various pleasures in their magnificent home. Lalita’s love for her husband and Lalit’s love for his wife were so great that they could not tolerate even a moment of separation.

One day, at the court of King Pundarika, many Gandharvas were singing and dancing, and Lalit was also singing there, but without his wife. Because Lalita was not beside him, Lalit’s voice, melody, steps, and words were all imperfect. Among the spectators was a serpent named Karkotaka, who knew the secret. He went to King Pundarika and complained about the true reason for Lalit’s behavior. The king then became extremely angry and cursed Lalit: “O sinful one! O fool! Being a slave to lust, you have disturbed the singing and dancing. Therefore I curse you to become a cannibal.”

O best of kings, cursed by King Pundarika, Lalit immediately turned into a great demon. When Lalita saw her husband in such a terrifying form, she became deeply distressed. In despair she passed her days wondering what to do and where to go.

One day, while wandering through a dense forest, they came upon the sacred ashrama of the sage Shringi on the summit of Mount Vindhya. Lalita immediately went there and offered respectful obeisances to the sage. Seeing the woman, the sage asked: “O beautiful one, who are you? Whose daughter are you? Why have you come here?” Lalita replied: “O great soul, I am the daughter of a Gandharva named Viradhanva. My name is Lalita. I have come here with my cursed husband. O great sage! My husband became a demon because of the curse of Pundarika, the king of the Gandharvas. O brahmana! I am deeply distressed to see his horrible and terrifying form. O my lord! Please tell me of a process of atonement by which my husband can become free from this curse. O best of brahmanas! Please give me instructions by which he may be delivered from this demonic condition.”

Hearing Lalita’s sorrowful plea, the great sage Shringi said: “O daughter of a Gandharva! In a few days there will be an Ekadashi called Kamada, which falls during the waxing moon in the month of March/April. By strictly observing this Ekadashi, all desires are fulfilled. O gentle woman! Following my instructions, observe this Ekadashi vow and transfer all the merit you acquire thereby to your husband. Then, by the influence of that merit, your husband will immediately become free from this curse.”

O king! Having received these instructions from the sage, Lalita joyfully observed the vow of this Ekadashi. On Dvadashi day, Lalita sat before the brahmanas and the Supreme Lord Vasudeva and declared: “I observed the vow of Kamada Ekadashi to free my husband from the curse. Now, by the influence of the merit I have accumulated, may my husband be freed from his demonic condition.” At that time her husband Lalit, who had been transformed into a demon, was present there. As soon as Lalita completed her prayer, her demon husband became free from all sins and regained his Gandharva form. Thereafter Lalit and Lalita lived happily.’

Lord Krishna continued: “O Maharaja Yudhishthira! O best of kings! Anyone who hears this wonderful narration of Kamada Ekadashi will certainly observe it to the best of his ability. There is no better Ekadashi vow than this Kamada Ekadashi, for it can free one even from the sin of killing a brahmana and from any curse.”

ekadashi.name: Varuthini Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Protects from misfortune, brings auspiciousness, and purifies bad karma.
ekadashi.story: Fasting on this day is praised as giving merit comparable to donating gold.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, April 13, 2026

The glories of Varuthini Ekadashi, which falls during the waning moon in the month of April/May, are described in the Bhavishyottara Purana in a conversation between Lord Krishna and Maharaja Yudhishthira.

Once Maharaja Yudhishthira said to Sri Krishna: “O Vasudeva! I offer my humble obeisances unto You. Now, please tell me about the Ekadashi that falls during the waning moon in the month of April/May. Tell me its name, influence, and glories.”

Lord Krishna replied: “My dear king, the name of this Ekadashi is Varuthini, and it bestows good fortune upon a person both in this life and in the next. By following this Ekadashi, a living being attains everlasting bliss, destroys the consequences of his sins, and obtains great good fortune. By observing this vow, an unfortunate wife becomes fortunate; a person attains happiness and prosperity both in this life and in the next; people become free from the cycle of birth and death; all the reactions to their sinful activities are nullified; and they attain devotional service to the Lord.

King Mandhata attained liberation by properly observing this Ekadashi. By observing Varuthini Ekadashi, one can attain the results of performing austerities for ten thousand years. The amount of merit acquired by giving forty kilograms of gold in charity during a solar eclipse at Kurukshetra is obtained simply by observing this Varuthini Ekadashi. O best of kings! It is better to give an elephant in charity than a horse. Better still is to give land, but even better is to give sesame seeds. Giving gold is better than giving sesame seeds, and giving grains is better still. There is no gift superior to grain! O best of kings! By giving grain in charity, one can satisfy the forefathers, the demigods, and all living beings. Learned men have declared that giving a daughter in marriage is equal to giving grain. The Supreme Lord Himself has compared the gift of grain with the gift of cows. Moreover, of all forms of charity, the highest is the distribution of knowledge.

By observing Varuthini Ekadashi, one can attain the results of all kinds of charity. A person who takes money in exchange for selling his daughter certainly commits a great sin, for which he will remain in hell until the final annihilation of the universe. Therefore, no one should ever accept wealth in exchange for a daughter. O king of kings! A householder who, driven by greed, sells his daughter becomes a cat in his next life. As for a person who decorates his daughter with jewels according to his means and gives her in marriage to a worthy bridegroom, even Chitragupta, the chief secretary of Yamaraja, is unable to calculate the virtue of such a person.

A person observing this Ekadashi should refrain from eating from a metal vessel and should not eat meat, peas, spinach, honey, food cooked by others, or more than once; nor should he engage in sexual relations, beginning from the day before Ekadashi.

On Ekadashi day, he should not gamble, sleep, chew betel nuts, brush his teeth, criticize anyone, gossip, converse with sinners, become angry, or tell lies.

On the day after Ekadashi, one should not eat from metal utensils, eat meat, masura gram, or honey; tell lies; exercise; perform heavy labor; eat more than once; engage in sexual relations; shave the head or face; apply oil to the body; or eat food cooked by others.

All the above should be avoided, otherwise the Ekadashi vow is broken. Along with the restrictions described above, certain prohibitions should be observed not only for these three days but always.

If a person observes the vow of Varuthini Ekadashi according to the rules and regulations, he becomes free from the reactions to all his sins and attains the supreme goal of life.

One who remains awake on Ekadashi day and worships Lord Janardana becomes free from all sins and attains the supreme goal of life. Anyone who hears or reads the glories of this Ekadashi obtains the results of giving one thousand cows in charity, becomes free from all sinful reactions, and attains the abode of Vishnu.”

ekadashi.name: Mohini Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Destroys illusion, relieves sorrow, and frees one from material attachments.
ekadashi.story: Connected with the Supreme Lord’s beautiful Mohini form.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, April 27, 2026

The glories of Mohini Ekadashi, which falls during the waxing moon in the month of April/May, are described in the Surya Purana.

Once Maharaja Yudhishthira addressed Lord Krishna: “O Janardana! What is the name of the Ekadashi that falls during the waxing moon in the month of April/May, and what is the process for observing this Ekadashi? What merit does a person acquire by following this Ekadashi? Please tell me about this in detail.”

Lord Krishna replied: “O son of Dharma! Please attentively hear from Me the story that the sage Vasishtha once told Lord Ramachandra. Once Lord Ramachandra asked the great sage Vasishtha: ‘O respected sage! I am experiencing great sorrow caused by separation from Sita, the daughter of King Janaka. Please tell me of a great vow by observing which all reactions to sinful activities and all sorrow disappear.’

The great sage Vasishtha, Ramachandra’s spiritual master, replied: ‘My dear Rama, Your intelligence is great, and You are endowed with faith. Your question brings benefit to all humanity. Simply by chanting and remembering Your auspicious holy names, all living beings can become purified and attain all auspiciousness. Nevertheless, for the benefit of ordinary people, I shall tell You about this great vow. O Lord Rama! The Ekadashi of the waxing moon in the month of April/May is known as Mohini Ekadashi. This Ekadashi is most auspicious. By observing this Ekadashi, all reactions to sinful activities, material suffering, and every kind of illusion are destroyed. Now please listen attentively, for I shall narrate the history of this most auspicious Ekadashi.

Once, on the bank of the sacred Sarasvati River, stood a beautiful city called Bhadravati. That city was ruled by a king named Dyutimana. O Lord Rama! This king was born in the lunar dynasty. He was tolerant and truthful. In the city lived a pious devotee of Lord Vishnu named Dhanapala. By occupation he was a vaishya, a merchant. For the benefit of ordinary people, this devotee Dhanapala built many dharmashalas, schools, temples of Lord Vishnu, hospitals, broad roads, and marketplaces. He also distributed food to the people, dug wells and ponds, and planted flower and fruit gardens. Thus he used his wealth for the welfare of all and thereby justified his name.

This pious devotee of Lord Vishnu, who was always peaceful, a benefactor of others, and engaged in devotional service to Vishnu, had five sons named Samana, Dyutimana, Medhavi, Sukriti, and Dhrishtabuddhi.

Dhrishtabuddhi was the most sinful of these brothers. He was a degraded man, kept company with scoundrels like himself, and was fond of prostitutes, gambling, and wine. He enjoyed killing and tormenting other living beings. Thus he committed every kind of sin and soon became the contemptible son of a most pious father and a disgrace to his family. He never showed respect to the demigods, guests, forefathers, or brahmanas. He constantly thought of how to commit sinful acts. The sinful and degraded Dhrishtabuddhi squandered his father’s wealth on various whims. He ate forbidden foods and constantly drank wine.

One day, seeing his shameless son walking in a public place with his arm around the shoulder of a prostitute, Dhanapala became desperate. That very day he drove his corrupt son out of the house. Dhrishtabuddhi lost the goodwill of everyone around him, including his father, mother, brothers, other relatives, and friends. Soon he lost his caste and became an object of universal contempt.

Having been cast into the street, Dhrishtabuddhi continued committing sins with the money he obtained by selling his clothes and ornaments. Soon even this came to an end. He had to go hungry and became emaciated. Now that Dhrishtabuddhi had become a homeless wanderer, his so-called friends and companions turned away from him. His anxiety increased. He had neither food nor clothing and was tormented by hunger. He began to think: ‘What shall I do now? Where shall I go? How shall I survive?’

After reflecting, he concluded that his only way out was theft. In search of plunder he began wandering through the city. Several times the king’s guards arrested him but released him, remembering his father’s virtues. Eventually he was arrested for a very serious theft. This time he was brought before the king, who imposed a severe punishment. The king said: ‘O sinful, foolish creature, you no longer have the right to remain in this kingdom, for you are a great sinner. I shall release you now, but please leave my kingdom immediately and go wherever you wish.’

Fearing that the next time he would receive an even more severe sentence, Dhrishtabuddhi left the kingdom. He traveled a great distance and reached a remote forest. In the forest he became so weak from hunger and thirst that he began killing animals and birds and eating their raw flesh. With bow and arrows in hand, he wandered through the forest, continuing to kill innocent animals. Thus Dhrishtabuddhi lived in the dark forest for several years, committing sins.

Dhrishtabuddhi always suffered and was filled with anxiety, but one day—apparently by the influence of pious deeds from his past—he came to the sacred ashrama of the great sage and ascetic Kaundinya. It was the month of Vaishakha, April/May, and the great sage Kaundinya was returning home after bathing in the Ganges. At that time, by the arrangement of providence, the grief-stricken Dhrishtabuddhi accidentally touched a drop of water that fell from the sage’s garment. By this, Dhrishtabuddhi was immediately freed from the reactions to his sinful activities.

With folded palms and great humility, he said to the sage Kaundinya: ‘O great brahmana, I am the worst of sinners. There is no sin I have not committed. Now, please tell me of the supreme atonement that even the lowest person like me can easily perform. As a result of committing innumerable sins, I have lost my home, wealth, relatives, and friends. I constantly suffer mental agony.’

Having heard Dhrishtabuddhi, the great sage Kaundinya, who felt sorrow upon seeing the suffering of others, said: ‘I shall tell you of a noble method by which you can easily and very quickly become free from the reactions to your sins. Please listen attentively.

Mohini Ekadashi, which falls during the waxing moon in the month of April/May, completely destroys the reactions to sins as great as Mount Sumeru and committed over many births. Therefore, you should faithfully observe this Ekadashi.’

Hearing these words of the great sage, Dhrishtabuddhi rejoiced and observed Ekadashi according to the sage’s rules and regulations. O best of kings! By observing this Mohini Ekadashi, the exceedingly sinful Dhrishtabuddhi soon became free from the reactions to his sins and, obtaining a divine body, returned to the all-auspicious abode of Lord Vishnu upon the back of Garuda. O Ramachandra! This vow destroys all kinds of illusion and the darkness of ignorance. Any merit gained by bathing in sacred waters, giving charity, or performing sacrifices cannot compare with the piety attained by observing this Mohini Ekadashi.’”

ekadashi.name: Apara Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Grants immense blessings and washes away grave sins such as violence and slander.
ekadashi.story: Purifies consciousness and brings auspiciousness and upliftment.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, May 13, 2026

Apara Ekadashi, which falls during the waning moon in the month of May/June, is described in the Brahmanda Purana in a conversation between Lord Krishna and Maharaja Yudhishthira.

Once Maharaja Yudhishthira asked Lord Krishna: “O Lord Krishna, O Janardana, what is the name of the Ekadashi that falls during the waning moon in the month of May/June, and what are its glories? Please tell me about it.”

Lord Krishna replied: “O Maharaja Yudhishthira, you have asked Me an intelligent question that brings benefit to everyone. The name of this Ekadashi is Apara. O king! This Ekadashi bestows great merit upon those who observe it and destroys all sinful reactions. By observing this Ekadashi, the reactions to many sinful activities are nullified, such as killing a brahmana, killing a cow, killing an embryo through abortion, criticizing others, illicit sexual relations, lying, giving false testimony, boasting, reciting the Vedas or teaching them for money, and falsifying the sacred scriptures.

A cheat, a false astrologer, and a fraudulent physician—such people are as sinful as a false witness. All such sinfulness is nullified by observing this Apara Ekadashi. Any kshatriya who abandons his duty and flees from the battlefield certainly goes to hell. If such a person observes this Ekadashi with faith, he too attains heaven.”

Lord Krishna continued: “O king! A disciple who, after receiving knowledge from his spiritual master, reviles him falls into great sin. Such a condemned sinner can become free from the reaction to this sin by observing Apara Ekadashi and thus attain the supreme goal of life. O king of kings! The result attained by bathing three times at Pushkara in the month of Kartika; the merit acquired by bathing at Prayaga in January when the sun enters the constellation of Capricorn; the results attained by observing the vow of Shivaratri in Kashi and worshiping the lotus feet of Vishnu in Gaya; the auspicious fruits of bathing in the Gautami River when Jupiter enters the constellation of Leo; and the fruits attained by visiting Kedarnatha during the Kumbha Mela, by visiting and worshiping at Badrinatha, by bathing at Kurukshetra during a solar eclipse, and by giving elephants, cows, gold, and land in charity—all these are easily attained by observing the vow of Apara Ekadashi.

This Ekadashi is like a sharp axe that cuts down the tree of sin and like a forest fire that burns all sins to ashes. It is like the radiant sun that dispels the darkness of sin and like a lion that devours the deer of sin in the forest of sins. O king! By observing this Apara Ekadashi and worshiping Lord Vishnu in His form as Trivikrama, a person attains the all-auspicious abode of Lord Vishnu. Anyone who hears or reads the glories of this Ekadashi becomes free from the reactions to all his sins. For the benefit of everyone, I have narrated these glories to you.”

ekadashi.name: Nirjala Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Grants the combined fruits of observing all other Ekadashis of the year.
ekadashi.story: This strict fast is observed without water and is known as the most austere Ekadashi.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, June 25, 2026

The description of Pandava Nirjala Ekadashi, which falls in the month of May/June, is found in the Brahma Vaivarta Purana in a conversation between Vyasadeva and Bhimasena.

Once Bhimasena, the younger brother of Yudhishthira, addressed the great sage Srila Vyasadeva: “O most learned and worshipable grandfather, please hear my request. My elder brother Yudhishthira, my mother Kuntidevi, my brothers Arjuna, Nakula, and Sahadeva, and Draupadi eat nothing on Ekadashi day. They, especially Yudhishthira, constantly tell me that I should fast on Ekadashi. But I always reply that I am unable to fast, although I know that fasting on Ekadashi is prescribed in the scriptures. Yet I cannot tolerate hunger and therefore cannot fast. I can give charity according to my means; I can worship Lord Keshava according to the rules and regulations, but I cannot fast. Therefore, please instruct me: how can I obtain the results of observing Ekadashi without fasting?”

Hearing these words of Bhimasena, Sri Vyasadeva said: “O Bhima! If you wish to attain heaven and avoid hell, then you must refrain from eating on the Ekadashi days of every month.”

Bhima said: “O great sage! I am unable to fast on the twenty-four Ekadashis each year as prescribed by the Lord. What to speak of fasting day and night—I cannot tolerate hunger for even a single moment. The fire of hunger known as vrika always burns in my stomach, and it can be extinguished only by abundant food. Gathering all my strength, I can fast for one day in a year. Therefore, please instruct me and tell me of a vow by following which I may attain benefit both in this life and in the next.”

Sri Vyasadeva replied: “O king! You have already heard from me about the Vedic religious principles and the duties of human beings. But in this age of Kali, no one is capable of following all these rules and restrictions. Therefore, I shall tell you of an exalted method by which you can attain wonderful results. This method is the essence of all the Puranas. Anyone who fasts on the Ekadashis of both the waxing and waning moons never goes to hell.”

Hearing Vyasadeva’s words, the mighty warrior Bhimasena became frightened and trembled like a banyan leaf. He said: “O grandfather! In that case, what shall I do? I am completely unable to fast twice a month throughout the whole year. Therefore, my lord, please instruct me how to observe a vow that bestows the greatest merit and all kinds of auspicious benefit.”

Sri Vyasadeva replied: “The Ekadashi that falls during the waxing moon in the month of May/June, when the sun is in either Taurus or Gemini, is called Nirjala Ekadashi. On this Ekadashi one must observe a complete fast, without even a drop of water. On this day one may perform achamana for purification by drinking an amount of water in which a mustard seed or a drop of gold could be immersed. The aforementioned quantity of water should be placed in the palm, formed so as to resemble a cow’s ear. If one drinks more or less than the specified amount, it is considered the same as drinking wine. One must not eat on this Ekadashi, otherwise the vow is broken. One must not even drink water from sunrise on Ekadashi until sunrise on Dvadashi. If one strictly observes this Ekadashi without water, one can attain the results of observing all the Ekadashis of the year. Early in the morning on Dvadashi, one should bathe and give gold and water in charity to the brahmanas. Thereafter one should happily eat together with the brahmanas.

O Bhimasena! Now please hear of the merits a person acquires by observing this Ekadashi. By following this Ekadashi, one can obtain the results of observing all the Ekadashis throughout the year.

Once Lord Vishnu, who holds the conch, disc, plough, and lotus flower, told me that if a person abandons various separate obligations, surrenders himself unto Him, and observes this Nirjala Ekadashi, which is very dear to Him, then he certainly becomes free from the consequences of all sinful activities. In this Kali-yuga, it is impossible to attain the supreme goal through charity or by following the rules of the smriti scriptures. Indeed, the religious principles of the Vedas are not effective in this age, which is contaminated by numerous faults.

O son of Vayu! What more shall I tell you? Eating is forbidden on every Ekadashi, and even water is forbidden on Nirjala Ekadashi. By observing this Ekadashi, a person obtains the results of visiting all holy places. At the time of death, such a person does not encounter the frightening Yamadutas; rather, he is met by the divine Vishnudutas, who carry him to the abode of Vishnu. If, after observing this Ekadashi, a person gives water and cows in charity, he becomes free from all sins.”

When the other Pandavas heard the glories of this Ekadashi, they too decided to observe it. From that day onward, this Ekadashi became known as Pandava Ekadashi or Bhima Ekadashi. If a person observes this Ekadashi, his sins, equal in magnitude to Mount Sumeru or Mount Mandara, are immediately burned to ashes. O king! Lord Krishna has declared that any pious activity—such as bathing in a sacred place, giving charity, reciting Vedic mantras, or performing sacrifices—when performed on this Ekadashi day yields extraordinary results. One who reads or hears narrations of the glories of this Ekadashi with devotion returns to the abode of Vaikuntha. Simply by hearing the glories of this Ekadashi, one attains the results of observing the Amavasya vow together with Pratipada and making ritual offerings to the forefathers during a solar eclipse.”

ekadashi.name: Yogini Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Grants relief from disease and serious ailments and purifies sins.
ekadashi.story: Frees one from sinful reactions and restores health.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, July 11, 2026

The glories of Yogini Ekadashi, which falls during the waning moon in the month of June/July, are described in the Brahma Vaivarta Purana in a conversation between Lord Krishna and Maharaja Yudhishthira.

Once Maharaja Yudhishthira addressed Krishna and said: “O Supreme Lord, O Madhusudana! I have heard the glories of Nirjala Ekadashi. Now I wish to hear about the Ekadashi that falls during the waning moon in the month of June/July.”

Lord Krishna said: “O king! I shall tell you about the Ekadashi that falls in the month of June/July. The name of this Ekadashi is Yogini. This Ekadashi immediately destroys all grave reactions to sinful activities and delivers a person from the ocean of material existence. O best of kings! Now I shall tell you a story from the Puranas to illustrate this truth.

Kubera, the king of Alakapuri, was a great devotee of Lord Shiva. He regularly worshiped Lord Shiva. The king had a gardener, a Yaksha named Hema. Hema’s wife was named Vishalakshi. Vishalakshi’s beauty was incomparable, and Hema was deeply attached to her. He regularly gathered flowers at Manasa Sarovara Lake and brought them to Kubera, the lord of the Yakshas, so that he could worship Lord Shiva with them.

One day, as usual, he gathered flowers, but instead of taking them to Kubera, he remained at home, bound by his love for his wife. O king! On that day Kubera was left without flowers. For six hours he waited in vain for Hema to appear. Without flowers he could not complete his worship of Lord Shiva. The enraged king immediately sent a messenger to Hema, wishing to know the reason for his absence.

After some time the messenger returned and said to the king: “O lord, Hema is enjoying the company of his wife at home.” When Kubera heard these words, his anger knew no bounds. He immediately ordered his servants to bring Hema before him. Realizing that he had made a mistake, Hema Mali felt ashamed and, trembling, appeared before Kubera. First the gardener respectfully bowed to him.

Kubera, whose whole body was trembling and whose eyes were red, said: “O sinful one! O destroyer of religious principles, you have neglected my Lord Sri Shankara, preferring your own sense enjoyment, and therefore I curse you. You shall be afflicted with white leprosy and forever deprived of the company of your dear wife. O degraded fool! Leave this place immediately.”

Cursed by Kubera, Hema Mali at once left Alakapuri and was born on earth. He was afflicted with white leprosy and suffered terribly. In this condition, experiencing extreme mental agony and deprived of food and water, he entered a dense and frightening forest. In that forest he suffered from hunger and thirst. By day he experienced no happiness, and by night he could not sleep. He suffered unbearably both day and night. However, because he had assisted in the service of Lord Shiva, his memory remained intact. Although he had committed various sins, he remembered his past actions, and his consciousness remained clear and alert.

After wandering in the forest for a long time, Hema finally, by great fortune, reached the Himalayan mountains. While wandering there, by the arrangement of providence he attained the good fortune of meeting the sage Markandeya, the best of ascetics, who had lived for seven kalpas. Feeling himself to be a great sinner, Hema Mali stood at some distance from the sage and offered him humble obeisances.

The kindhearted sage Markandeya called the leper to him and asked: “How did you become afflicted with this terrible disease? What sins did you commit that brought you into such a miserable condition?” Hema Mali replied: “O great sage! I am the gardener of Kubera, the king of the Yakshas. My name is Hema Mali. I regularly gathered flowers at Manasa Sarovara Lake and offered them to my lord Kubera. With those flowers Kubera worshiped Lord Shiva.”

Hema Mali then told the sage the entire story of his misfortunes and added: “But now I do not know why this unfortunate soul has suddenly gained the good fortune of meeting a great personality like you. I have heard that the hearts of saints are always compassionate and that such saints are always engaged in serving others. O great sage! Desiring to attain good fortune, this fallen soul surrenders unto you. Please be kind and save it.”

The great sage Markandeya compassionately replied: “O gardener! I shall instruct you about the most auspicious and beneficial vow. You should observe the Ekadashi vow known as Yogini, which falls during the waning moon in the month of June/July. By the merit gained through observing such a vow, you will certainly become free from the curse of leprosy.”

Hearing this instruction from the great sage, Hema Mali rejoiced and gratefully bowed to Markandeya. He then properly observed the sacred Ekadashi vow according to the sage’s directions, and by doing so regained his divine form. Thereafter he returned home and was reunited with his wife. The result attained by feeding eighty-eight thousand brahmanas can be attained by observing this Yogini Ekadashi. This Ekadashi destroys all reactions to sin and bestows great piety.”

ekadashi.name: Devashayani Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Marks the beginning of Chaturmasya and opens the way to spiritual refinement.
ekadashi.story: The day when Lord Vishnu begins His four-month rest on the cosmic serpent Shesha.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, July 25, 2026

Shayana Ekadashi, also known as Devashayani or Padma Ekadashi, is described in the Bhavishyottara Purana in a conversation between Lord Krishna and Maharaja Yudhishthira.

Once Maharaja Yudhishthira addressed Krishna and said: “O Keshava! What is the name of the Ekadashi that falls during the waxing moon in the month of June/July? Which deity is worshiped on this sacred day, and what are the rules for observing this Ekadashi? Please tell me about this in detail.”

Lord Krishna replied: “O lord of this world! Narada Muni once asked Lord Brahma this very question. Now, please hear from Me the wonderful story that Lord Brahma told Narada Muni.

Once Narada Muni, the eloquent speaker and best of sages, addressed Lord Brahma and said: ‘O father! What is the name of the Ekadashi that falls during the waxing moon in the month of June/July? Please tell me how I should observe this Ekadashi in order to satisfy the Supreme Lord Vishnu.’

Lord Brahma replied: ‘In this material world there is no vow as sacred as the Ekadashi vow. It is extremely important to observe Ekadashi in order to become free from the reactions to sins. A person who does not observe Ekadashi in this world will inevitably go to hell. The Ekadashi that falls during the waxing moon in the month of June/July is called Devashayani or Padma Ekadashi. To satisfy the Supreme Lord Hrishikesha, one should observe this Ekadashi.

The Purana tells that there once lived a saintly emperor named Mandhata, who ruled the entire world. He was born in the dynasty of the sun-god. The king’s authority was great, and he always stood on the side of truth. In the kingdom of this pious king there was no famine, drought, or disease of any kind. All his subjects lived happily, free from anxiety and prosperous in every respect. The king’s treasury contained no wealth acquired by unrighteous means.

After many years of such happy life, no rain fell in the kingdom for three consecutive years. Famine began, and the people suffered. Because of the lack of food, the performance of various sacrifices and the study of the Vedas ceased.

Then all the subjects approached the king: “O king! Please listen to our words. The scriptures call water ‘nara.’ The Supreme Lord dwells in ‘ayana.’ Therefore the Supreme Lord is called Narayana. The Supreme Lord Vishnu becomes the clouds. He is the sole cause of rain. By rain, food grains are produced; all living beings depend upon rain. Now, because of the lack of grain, your subjects are suffering and dying. O best of kings! Please find a means to free us from suffering and restore peace and prosperity.”

The king replied: “Everything you have said is true. Grains are considered Brahman. The entire world and all living beings depend upon grain. The Puranas and other scriptures clearly state that because of sins committed by the king, both he and his subjects suffer. Although it is difficult for me to judge my own faults, I shall nevertheless do everything possible to help my subjects.”

Having said this, King Mandhata gathered an army and, after offering obeisances to Brahma, entered the forest. In the forest he regularly visited the ashramas of great sages and ascetics. One day, while wandering through the forest, by the arrangement of providence the king met the great sage Angira, the son of Brahma. The sage Angira was radiant like Brahma, and all four directions were illuminated by his effulgence. As soon as the king saw him, he immediately descended from his palanquin and offered respectful obeisances at the sage’s feet. Then the king, with folded hands, offered prayers. The sage replied with kind words and blessed the king. Afterward the sage inquired about the reason for the king’s visit and the condition of affairs in his kingdom.

The king replied: “O lord! I have ruled my kingdom according to religious principles; nevertheless, for the past three years there has been no rain in my kingdom. As a result, my subjects are suffering. I have been unable to discover the cause of this distress. Today I have come to your lotus feet. Please tell me how my subjects can live peacefully and thus attain the highest good.”

The sage Angira replied: “O king! The present age, Satya-yuga, is the best of all yugas. In this yuga people worship the Supreme Brahman. In this yuga they live according to religious principles. In this yuga no one except brahmanas should perform austerities.

Despite this restriction, a certain shudra residing in your kingdom is performing austerities. As a result of this improper conduct, you are facing the consequence in the form of drought. Therefore, you should try to kill him. If he is executed, peace and prosperity will return to your kingdom.”

The king replied: “O great sage, it is unthinkable for me to kill an innocent person who is performing austerities. Please advise me of another solution.” The sage said: “O king, in that case, observe the sacred Ekadashi known as Padma or Devashayani, which falls during the waxing moon in the month of June/July. By the influence of this vow, rain will certainly fall in your kingdom. This Ekadashi bestows all auspiciousness and every perfection. O king! You should observe this Ekadashi together with all your subjects.”

Hearing these encouraging words of the great sage, the king bowed to him and returned to the palace. Thereafter, in the month of Ashadha, in June/July, the king, together with his relatives and subjects, properly observed this auspicious Padma or Shayana Ekadashi. By the influence of this vow, rain fell throughout his kingdom. Soon, by the mercy of Lord Hrishikesha, mountains of grain arose, and all the king’s subjects lived happily.

Therefore, it is everyone’s duty to observe this sacred Ekadashi. This Ekadashi bestows happiness and liberation upon all. By hearing and reading the glories of this Ekadashi, all reactions to sinful activities are destroyed. This Ekadashi is also known as Vishnu Shayani Ekadashi. Desiring to satisfy Lord Vishnu, devotees observe this Ekadashi with special zeal. They do not aspire for material enjoyment or liberation; rather, they pray for pure devotional service to the Lord.

The famous vow of Chaturmasya begins with this Ekadashi. Devotees observe this Chaturmasya vow by hearing about the Lord and glorifying Him for four months, beginning from the day Lord Hari lies down upon His bed and ending on the day He rises from it.’”

Maharaja Yudhishthira said to Lord Krishna: “O Krishna! Please tell me how this Sri Vishnu Shayana or Chaturmasya Vrata should be observed.”

Lord Krishna replied: “O king! When the sun remains in the sign of Cancer, Sri Madhusudana, the Lord of the entire universe, lies down upon His bed, and when the sun enters the sign of Libra, the Lord awakens. The vow of Chaturmasya begins on Shayana Ekadashi. O King Yudhishthira! After bathing, one should dress Lord Vishnu in yellow garments. Then a bed should be prepared and covered with white sheets upon which the Lord will rest. First, the Lord should be bathed with five substances, such as yogurt, milk, ghee, honey, and sweet water. Worthy brahmanas should perform this. Thereafter the Lord should be dressed, and His body anointed with fragrant paste. Then one should worship the Lord with devotion, offering Him incense, ghee lamps, and flowers.

One may begin observing the Chaturmasya vow on any one of these days: Ekadashi, Dvadashi, Purnima, Ashtami, or Sankranti, when the sun enters the sign of Cancer. The Chaturmasya vow ends on the Dvadashi that falls on the day after Utthana Ekadashi in the month of Kartika.

A person who observes the Chaturmasya vow while remembering Lord Vishnu goes to the abode of Lord Vishnu, seated upon an aerial vehicle radiant like the sun. Anyone who cleans the Lord’s temple and the temple courtyard, decorates them with flowers and plants, and feeds brahmanas according to his means, attains, upon completion of the vow, happiness lasting for seven lifetimes. By offering ghee lamps to the Lord throughout this vow, one can attain good fortune and prosperity. One who chants the Gayatri mantra in the Lord’s temple 108 times, three times daily—morning, noon, and evening—never again has to commit sins. Lord Vyasa becomes pleased with such a person, and that person returns to the abode of Vishnu.

Anyone who, at the end of the Chaturmasya period, gives twenty-eight or 108 pots filled with sesame seeds to intelligent brahmanas becomes free from the reactions to sins accumulated through the mind and speech. He becomes free from all diseases, and intelligent children are born to him.

During the four months while Lord Janardana rests, one should not sleep on a bed or engage in sexual relations. One should eat only in the evening, eat once a day, or eat whatever comes of its own accord. One who sings and dances for Lord Vishnu during Chaturmasya goes to the world of the Gandharvas. One who gives up eating molasses is blessed with sons and grandsons. If a person gives up oil, he becomes beautiful and his enemies perish. By giving up bitter, pungent, sour, sweet, and salty dishes, one can become free from deformity and foul bodily odor. Those who give up flowers go to heaven and become Vidyadharas. Giving up betel nuts brings immediate freedom from all diseases. If one eats from an empty flower, one can attain the heaven of Indra. If, for Krishna’s pleasure, one gives up milk and yogurt, one can return to the supreme abode, Goloka. A person who does not cut his nails or shave his head during Chaturmasya attains the good fortune of touching the lotus feet of Vishnu. One who circumambulates the Lord’s temple returns to the Lord’s abode in an aerial vehicle drawn by swans.”

ekadashi.name: Kamika Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Purifies even grave sins, grants happiness, and gives protection.
ekadashi.story: Bestows blessings on all who sincerely seek shelter at the Lord’s feet.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, August 9, 2026

Kamika Ekadashi is described in the Brahma Vaivarta Purana in a conversation between Lord Krishna and Maharaja Yudhishthira.

Maharaja Yudhishthira said: “O Supreme Lord Krishna! I have heard from You about the glories of Devashayani Ekadashi. Now I would like to hear about the Ekadashi that falls during the waning moon in the month of July/August. O Lord, please be kind to me and tell me of its glories.”

Lord Krishna replied: “O king! Please attentively hear the description of this sacred Ekadashi vow, which removes all sins. Once, in ancient times, Narada Muni asked Lord Brahma the very same question. He also asked which deity should be worshiped on this day and about the process of observing this Ekadashi.

Lord Brahma, the spiritual master of the entire universe, replied to him: ‘The Ekadashi that falls during the waning moon in the month of July/August is called Kamika Ekadashi. By hearing the glories of this Ekadashi, one attains the result of performing the Vajapeya sacrifice.
