On this auspicious day one should worship Lord Vishnu, who holds the conch, disc, club, and lotus in His hands. The results attained by studying the sacred scriptures and bathing in such holy places as the Ganges, Kashi, Naimisharanya, and Pushkara are attained simply by worshiping Lord Vishnu on this day. The result that cannot be attained even by bathing at Kedarnatha, at Kurukshetra, or during a solar eclipse is easily attained by worshiping Lord Krishna on this day. Therefore, it is everyone’s duty to strictly observe this Kamika Ekadashi by worshiping Lord Vishnu.

Just as water cannot touch a lotus leaf, by the influence of this Kamika Ekadashi a person can remain untouched by sin. Anyone who worships Lord Hari with tulasi leaves becomes free from all sins. Simply by beholding tulasi, all reactions to sinful activities are destroyed; by touching tulasi, the body is purified; by offering prayers to tulasi, all diseases disappear; by bathing tulasi, fear of Yamaraja, the Lord of Death, vanishes; by planting tulasi, a person becomes fortunate enough to live in the association of Lord Krishna; and by offering tulasi leaves at the feet of the Supreme Lord, one attains pure devotional service. Even Chitragupta is unable to calculate the merit of one who offers obeisances and a ghee lamp to such tulasi on Ekadashi day. The sin of killing a brahmana or an embryo is nullified, and this is no more than a secondary result of observing this Kamika Ekadashi. One who hears or reads the glories of this Ekadashi with faith will certainly attain the abode of Lord Vishnu.’”

ekadashi.name: Pavitropana Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Blesses one with righteous children, purifies the family line, and brings welfare.
ekadashi.story: Helps remove past-life curses and obtain pious offspring.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, August 23, 2026

The glories of Pavitropana Ekadashi are described in the Bhavishyottara Purana in a conversation between Lord Krishna and Maharaja Yudhishthira.

Once Maharaja Yudhishthira addressed Krishna with these words: “O Madhusudana, killer of the demon Madhu! What is the name of the Ekadashi that falls during the waxing moon in the month of July/August, and what are its glories? Please tell me about this in detail.”

Lord Krishna replied: “O king! This sacred Ekadashi is called Pavitra Ekadashi. Now, please attentively hear the narration of this Ekadashi, which destroys the reactions to all sins. By hearing the glories of this Ekadashi, one attains the results of the Vajapeya sacrifice.

In ancient times, at the beginning of Dvapara-yuga, there lived a king named Mahijit, who ruled a kingdom called Mahishmatipuri. Because the king had no sons, he found no joy in either affairs of state or amusements. A married man who has no son experiences not the slightest happiness either in this life or in the next. For many years the king unsuccessfully tried to become the father of a son, but he was not fortunate enough to obtain such a jewel-like son, the source of all joy.

Realizing the pitiable circumstances in which he found himself, one day the king summoned his subjects, whom he regarded as his own children, to the royal assembly and said to them: “O dear subjects, I have never committed sinful acts in my life; I have not filled my treasury with wealth acquired by unrighteous means; I have not taken the wealth of brahmanas or demigods. On the contrary, I conquered this world by following the code of honor, I cared for you as my own children, I always punished even those close to me, such as my brother and relatives, without hesitation, judging them according to their deeds, and I showed proper respect even to an enemy if he was noble and pious. O brahmanas, although I have followed such a religious path, why am I deprived of a son? Please reflect upon the reasons for this and advise me.”

After hearing the sorrowful words of King Mahijit, the king’s brahmana counselors conferred and decided that, for the king’s benefit, they would go to the forest and visit the ashramas of great sages who knew the past, present, and future. And so they did. They entered the forest and began visiting the ashramas of great sages scattered throughout it.

At last they met Lomasa Muni, who was performing severe austerities. His body was spiritual and full of bliss. He observed strict fasting, controlled his senses, knew the science of the Eternal Principles of Religion, was learned in all the scriptures, and his lifespan equaled that of Brahma. Whenever one kalpa of Brahma came to an end, one hair, or loma, fell from his body, and therefore the sage was called Lomasa. The sage Lomasa knew the past, present, and future.

The king’s counselors offered obeisances to the sage and humbly said: “O great sage! By our great good fortune we have met a great soul like you.” The sage Lomasa asked: “Who are you? Why have you come here? Why do you praise me?” The brahmanas replied: “O great sage! We have come to you to dispel our doubts. O lord! Our king has no sons. We are his subjects, and the king treats us as his own children. We are sorrowful to see our lord’s grief. O best of brahmanas, we wish to perform severe austerities here. By our king’s great good fortune, today we have met a great personality like you. The darshan of a great personality enables one to attain every perfection. Please give us instructions by following which our childless king may obtain a son.”

Hearing these sincere prayers, the sage Lomasa entered deep meditation for a moment and immediately saw the previous life of King Mahijit. He then said that in his previous birth the king had been a poor vaishya, a merchant. He had committed sinful acts. Once, while traveling from village to village and trading, he became thirsty. It was noon on Dvadashi in the month of July. Soon he found a beautiful lake and decided to drink from it. At that time a cow with her calf came to the shore of the lake to drink. As soon as the cow tried to do so, the merchant immediately drove her away and drank first himself. In this way the merchant committed a sin. Later, by virtue of his merits, the merchant was born as King Mahijit, but he had no son.

Hearing these words of the great sage, the king’s counselors said: “O great sage! The Puranas state that pious merit destroys the reactions to sinful activities. Therefore, please give us instructions by which all the reactions to the king’s sins will be destroyed and he will be able to become the father of a son.”

The great sage Lomasa replied: “There is a famous and auspicious Ekadashi known as Pavitra Ekadashi, which falls during the waxing moon in the month of July/August. All of you and the king should properly observe this Ekadashi. If you follow my advice, the king will certainly be blessed with a son.”

Hearing these words of the sage Lomasa, all the king’s counselors immediately became happy and satisfied. They bowed to the sage and returned home. Then they met King Mahijit and told him in detail everything they had heard from the great sage Lomasa. Later, when the proper time arrived, the king’s counselors remembered the sage’s advice and, together with the king, properly observed the vow of Pavitra Ekadashi. On Dvadashi day, as the sage had advised, the counselors transferred all the accumulated merit to the king. By the influence of this merit, the queen became pregnant and, in due course, gave birth to a beautiful son.

O King Yudhishthira, anyone who observes this sacred Ekadashi becomes free from the reactions to sinful activities and becomes happy both in this life and in the next. Anyone who hears the glories of this Ekadashi attains the happiness arising from fatherhood in this life and returns to God in the next life.”

ekadashi.name: Annada Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Destroys sins and the reactions of past sinful acts.
ekadashi.story: Connected with the story of King Harishchandra, who regained his kingdom through this fast.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, September 7, 2026

The glories of Annada, or Aja, Ekadashi are described in the Brahma Vaivarta Purana in a conversation between Lord Krishna and Maharaja Yudhishthira.

Maharaja Yudhishthira said: “O Krishna! What is the name of the Ekadashi that falls during the waning moon in the month of August/September? Please be kind and tell me about it.”

Lord Krishna replied: “O king! Hear Me with full attention. The name of this auspicious Ekadashi, which removes all sins, is Annada Ekadashi. One who observes this Ekadashi and worships Lord Hrishikesha, the master of the senses, becomes free from the reactions to his sinful activities.

In ancient times there lived an emperor named Harishchandra. He was a most truthful and honest man. It so happened that he desired to keep his word, and because of this the king lost his kingdom. He was even forced to sell himself, his wife, and his son into servitude. O king! This pious emperor became the servant of a dog-eater. Nevertheless, he continued to adhere unwaveringly to his principles of life.

By the order of his master, the dog-eater, he began removing clothes from dead bodies at cremation grounds and accepting them as wages. Despite such a pitiable condition, he continued to remain virtuous and truthful. Many years passed in this way. Then one day the king, feeling miserable, began to reflect: “What shall I do? Where shall I go? How shall I attain deliverance?”

Understanding that the king was experiencing great sorrow, the sage Gautama came to him. On seeing the great sage, the king thought that Lord Brahma, the creator, had created the brahmanas for the welfare of other people. Then the king offered respectful obeisances to the best of brahmanas and stood before him with folded hands. He told the sage the sorrowful story of his life.

After hearing the king, the great sage Gautama was greatly astonished and gave the king the following instructions: “O king! Annada Ekadashi, which falls during the waning moon in the month of August/September, is supremely auspicious and removes all sins. Your good fortune is that this Ekadashi is approaching. You should observe this Ekadashi by fasting and remaining awake throughout the night. As a result, all the reactions to your sinful activities will soon be destroyed. O best of kings, it is only by your influence that I have come here.” Having instructed King Harishchandra, the great sage Gautama disappeared. Thereafter, according to the sage’s instructions, the king observed the vow of Annada Ekadashi and became free from all sinful reactions.

Lord Krishna concluded: “O lion-like king! The wonderful influence of this Ekadashi is such that by its power a person is immediately freed from the suffering he was destined to endure for many, many years. By the influence of this Ekadashi, King Harishchandra regained his wife, and his dead son returned to life. Rejoicing, the demigods began to beat drums, and a shower of flowers fell from the sky. Thereafter, again by the influence of this Ekadashi, the king enjoyed his sovereignty without obstruction. In the end, the king went to the spiritual world together with his relatives, associates, and subjects.

O king! Anyone who observes this Ekadashi becomes free from sins and goes to the spiritual world. By hearing and reading the glories of this Ekadashi, one attains the results of a horse sacrifice.”

ekadashi.name: Parivartini Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Purifies all sins and is praised as giving the fruit of offering a thousand cows.
ekadashi.story: The day when Lord Vishnu turns to His other side during His divine sleep.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, September 22, 2026

The glories of Parshva Ekadashi, which is also known as Parivartini Ekadashi or Vamana Ekadashi, are described in the Brahma Vaivarta Purana in a conversation between Lord Krishna and Maharaja Yudhishthira.

Maharaja Yudhishthira asked Lord Krishna: “What is the name of the Ekadashi that falls during the waxing moon in the month of August/September? How should this Ekadashi be observed, and what benefit can be obtained by observing it? Please tell me about this in detail.”

Lord Krishna replied: “O king! The Ekadashi that occurs during the waxing moon in the month of August/September is called Parshva Ekadashi. This Ekadashi is very auspicious; it bestows liberation and destroys all sins. By hearing the glories of this Ekadashi, the reactions to all sinful activities are destroyed. The merit attained by observing this Ekadashi cannot be attained even by performing the Vajapeya sacrifice. This Ekadashi is also known as Jayanti. One who worships Lord Vamanadeva with devotion on this day himself becomes an object of worship for the inhabitants of the three worlds. A person who worships lotus-eyed Lord Vishnu by offering Him lotus flowers certainly returns to the abode of the Lord. On this Ekadashi, the sleeping Lord turns from His left side onto His right. That is why this Ekadashi is known as Parshva Parivartini, literally, ‘turning from one side to the other,’ Ekadashi.”

Maharaja Yudhishthira said: “O Janardana! Although I have heard Your description, I still have doubts. O Lord of lords! How do You sleep, and how do You turn over? What procedures must be followed during Chaturmasya? What should people do while You sleep? Why did You bind Bali Maharaja with ropes? O my Lord! Please give me a detailed answer and remove my doubts.”

Lord Krishna replied: “O lion-like king! In Treta-yuga there lived a great devotee named Bali. Although born in a demonic family, he regularly worshiped Me and offered various prayers. He also worshiped the brahmanas and performed various sacrifices. Soon he gained such power that he defeated Indra, the king of heaven, and seized the heavenly kingdom.

Then Indra, together with the other demigods and sages, approached Me. Hearing their prayer, I assumed the form of a dwarf, Vamana, and appeared at the sacrificial arena of King Bali dressed as a young brahmachari. I asked Bali to give Me as much land as could be measured by three steps. Hearing My request for only three steps of land, Bali asked whether I desired something more, but I showed My determination to accept only this. Without further deliberation, King Bali and his wife Vindhyavali gave Me three measures of land.”

Being the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Vamanadeva gradually began to expand in size. With His first step He covered the seven lower worlds, and with His second, all the planets. Expanding further, He covered the entire sky. When Vamanadeva asked where He could place His third step, King Bali, with folded hands, offered his own head.

Satisfied by his humility, I blessed him: “You will always live with Me.” On the day of this Ekadashi, which falls during the waxing moon in the month of August/September, the deity of Vamanadeva was installed in King Bali’s residence. Another form of Mine was installed upon the bed of Ananta Shesha in the Ocean of Milk.

The Supreme Lord sleeps for four months, beginning with Shayana Ekadashi and continuing until Utthana Ekadashi. During these four months, one should worship the Lord with special attention. Every Ekadashi should be properly observed. By observing this Ekadashi, one attains the result of performing one thousand horse sacrifices.”

ekadashi.benefits: Grants liberation to ancestors and purifies negative karma.

Ekadashi, October 6, 2026

The glories of Indira Ekadashi are described in the Brahma Vaivarta Purana in a conversation between Lord Krishna and Maharaja Yudhishthira.

Maharaja Yudhishthira said: “O Krishna! O Madhusudana! O killer of the demon Madhu! What is the name of the Ekadashi that falls during the waning moon in the month of September/October? What are the rules and restrictions for observing this Ekadashi, and what merit can be acquired by observing it?”

Lord Krishna replied: “This sacred Ekadashi is called Indira Ekadashi. By observing this Ekadashi, one can deliver one’s fallen ancestors from hell and become free from the reactions to all sinful activities. O king!

Once there lived a ruler named Indrasena. He lived in Satya-yuga and was skilled in subduing his enemies. He ruled his kingdom of Mahishmatipuri, which prospered in every respect. He was surrounded by children and grandchildren, and everyone lived happily.

The king was attached to devotional service to Vishnu. Being a devotee absorbed in spiritual knowledge, he spent his time chanting the holy names of Sri Govinda, the bestower of liberation. One day, while the king was seated upon his throne, Sri Narada Muni unexpectedly appeared before him, descending from heaven. Seeing the great sage Narada, the king immediately rose and offered him respectful obeisances. Thereafter the king properly worshiped the sage, offering him sixteen ingredients. Seated comfortably, the sage asked Indrasena: “O great king! Are your subjects happy and prosperous? Is your mind fixed in religious principles? Are you rendering devotional service to Vishnu?”

The king replied: “O best of sages! By your mercy, everything in the kingdom is well and auspicious. Today my life has become successful by your darshan, and my sacrifices have borne fruit. O sage among the demigods! Please tell me the reason for your visit.”

Hearing these humble words of the king, Narada Muni said: “O lion-like king! Hear of a wondrous event that happened to me. O best of kings!

Once I traveled from the abode of Lord Brahma to the abode of Yamaraja. When I reached his kingdom, Yamaraja respectfully welcomed me and properly worshiped me. After I had been comfortably seated, I offered prayers to the pious and truthful Yamaraja. In Yamaraja’s assembly I saw your father, endowed with great piety. Because he had broken a vow, your father was forced to remain there. O king! He gave me a message for you.

He said: ‘Indrasena, the king of Mahishmatipuri, is my son. O lord, please tell him that because of certain sinful activities committed in a previous life, I now reside in the abode of Yamaraja. Therefore, he should observe the vow of Indira Ekadashi and offer the merit to me. Then I shall be freed from my present circumstances.’

Narada Muni continued: “O king! This is your father’s request to you. Therefore, in order to help your father attain the spiritual world, you should observe the vow of Indira Ekadashi.”

Then King Indrasena said: “O sage among the demigods, now kindly explain to me the procedure for observing this Indira Ekadashi.”

Narada Muni replied: “On the day before Ekadashi, one should rise early in the morning, bathe, and make a ritual offering to the ancestors for their satisfaction. On that day one should eat only once and sleep on the floor at night. On Ekadashi day one should rise at dawn, brush one’s teeth, wash one’s hands, and bathe. Thereafter one should vow not to engage in any material enjoyment and thus observe a complete fast. In addition, one should pray to the Lord with these words: ‘O lotus-eyed Lord, I take shelter in You.’”

ekadashi.name: Pasankusha Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Grants wealth, health, fulfilled desires, and destroys sins.
ekadashi.story: A special day on which sincere fasting protects one from lower destinations.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, October 22, 2026

The glories of Pasankusha Ekadashi, which falls during the waxing moon in the month of September/October, are described in the Brahma Vaivarta Purana in a conversation between Lord Krishna and Maharaja Yudhishthira.

Maharaja Yudhishthira asked: “O Madhusudana, what is the name of the Ekadashi that falls during the waxing moon in the month of September/October? Please be kind and tell me about it.”

Lord Krishna replied: “O best of kings! This Ekadashi is called Pasankusha Ekadashi. Now, please hear about this Ekadashi, which destroys all sins. Some people call this Ekadashi Papankusha Ekadashi. On this Ekadashi day one should worship Lord Padmanabha. This Ekadashi bestows heavenly enjoyment, liberation, and everything desired upon those who observe it. By chanting the holy names of Lord Vishnu, one can acquire the merit of visiting all the holy places on earth. If a conditioned soul, instead of committing various sins, takes shelter of Lord Hari, who is expert in delivering fallen souls, and offers obeisances unto Him, that soul does not go to hell.

Vaishnavas who criticize Lord Shiva and Shaivas who criticize Lord Vishnu undoubtedly go to hell. The result attained by performing one thousand horse sacrifices or one hundred Rajasuya sacrifices cannot equal even one-sixteenth of the merit attained by observing this Ekadashi.

There is no merit in this world equal to the merit of observing Ekadashi. Therefore, no other day is as sacred as this Ekadashi day, which is very dear to Lord Padmanabha. O king! As soon as a person becomes unable to observe Ekadashi, sins begin to dwell within his body. This Ekadashi bestows heavenly enjoyment, liberation, freedom from disease, beautiful women, and grain upon its followers. O protector of the earth! If a person observes this Ekadashi and remains awake throughout the night of Ekadashi, he easily attains the abode of Lord Vishnu.”

Lord Krishna continued: “O best of kings! By observing the vow of this Ekadashi, one can save ten generations of ancestors on the mother’s side, ten generations on the father’s side, and ten generations on the wife’s side. If a person observes this Ekadashi in childhood, youth, or old age, he does not encounter the sufferings of material existence. A person who strictly observes this Pasankusha or Papankusha Ekadashi becomes free from the reactions to all his sinful activities and, at the end of life, returns to the abode of Lord Vishnu.

If a person gives gold, sesame seeds, land, cows, grain, water, canopies, or footwear in charity, then at the end of life he returns to the abode of Lord Vishnu. Anyone who spends his days without performing pious activities is like a dead man, although he breathes. O best of kings! A person who digs wells and lakes for the benefit of others, gives land and buildings in charity, and performs other pious activities, such as arranging sacrifices, does not become an object of Yamaraja’s punishment. Only by piety do people live long, become wealthy, take birth in aristocratic families, and become free from disease. The meaning is that the direct result of observing Ekadashi is the attainment of devotional service to Krishna, while the indirect result is the attainment of temporary material benefits.”

ekadashi.name: Rama Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Purifies grave sins and leads one toward Lord Vishnu.
ekadashi.story: Grants devotion and strong spiritual aspiration.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, November 5, 2026 — Rama Ekadashi

The glories of Rama Ekadashi are described in the Brahma Vaivarta Purana in a conversation between Lord Krishna and Maharaja Yudhishthira.

Maharaja Yudhishthira said: “O Janardana! What is the name of the Ekadashi that falls during the waning moon in the month of October/November? Please tell me about it.”

Lord Krishna replied: “O lion among kings! The name of this Ekadashi is Rama Ekadashi; it destroys the consequences of all sinful activities. Now, please hear the glories of this sacred Ekadashi.

In ancient times there lived a famous king named Muchukunda. He was a good friend of Indra, the lord of heaven. He was also friends with such personalities as Yamaraja, Varuna, Kubera, and Vibhishana. The king was very truthful and attached to devotional service to Lord Vishnu. He ruled his kingdom according to all the provisions of the code of law. In time, King Muchukunda became the father of a daughter.

She was named Chandrabhaga after the most excellent river Chandrabhaga. The girl was given in marriage to an attractive young man named Shobhana, who was the son of Chandrasena.

One day Shobhana came to the house of his father-in-law on Ekadashi day. Chandrabhaga became anxious and thought: “O my Lord! What will happen now? My husband is very weak and cannot tolerate hunger. Moreover, my father is very strict. On the day before Ekadashi, my father usually sends his servant to announce that no one should eat on Ekadashi day.”

When Shobhana heard of this custom, he said to his dear wife: “Beloved! What shall I do now? How can I arrange matters so that my life is protected and the king’s order is fulfilled?”

Chandrabhaga replied: “O my lord! What to speak of human beings, when even elephants, horses, and other animals are not allowed to eat on this day! O husband, how then can human beings eat? O respected husband! If you absolutely must eat today, then you should return home. Therefore, think carefully and make your decision.”

Hearing his wife’s words, Shobhana remarked: “Your words are true, but I desire to observe this Ekadashi. Whatever is destined for me will certainly come to pass.” Thinking in this way, Shobhana decided to observe this sacred Ekadashi. He was tormented by hunger and thirst.

When the sun set, all the Vaishnavas and pious people became happy. O lion among kings! They happily spent the entire night worshiping the Supreme Lord and chanting His names. But for Shobhana the night was so difficult that he died just before sunrise.

King Muchukunda performed a splendid ceremony, and Shobhana’s body was cremated upon a pyre of sandalwood. Obeying her father’s will, Chandrabhaga did not burn herself on the funeral pyre—in other words, she did not die with her husband. After all the Shraddha rituals were completed, Chandrabhaga remained living in her father’s house.

O king! At that time, by the influence of Rama Ekadashi, Shobhana became the king of the beautiful city of Devapura, situated on the summit of Mount Mandara. He began to live in a luxurious residence whose pillars were made of gold and decorated with precious stones, while the walls were inlaid with crystal and natural gems. Above his head was a beautiful white canopy adorned with gold and jewels. His ears were decorated with earrings, his neck with a precious necklace, and his arms with golden bracelets. Thus adorned, Shobhana sat upon a royal throne. He was constantly served by Gandharvas and apsaras. He resembled Indra, the king of heaven.

One day a brahmana named Somasharma, a resident of Muchukundapura, arrived in Shobhana’s kingdom while traveling through holy places. Considering Shobhana to be the son-in-law of King Muchukunda, the brahmana approached him.

As soon as the king saw the brahmana, he stood before him with folded hands and then offered him respectful obeisances. Thereafter Shobhana inquired from the brahmana about his welfare and the welfare of his father-in-law King Muchukunda, his wife Chandrabhaga, and all the residents of Muchukundapura. The brahmana informed the king that all of them were living happily and peacefully. With great astonishment, the brahmana said to the king: “O king, I have never seen such a beautiful city. Please tell me how you obtained such a kingdom.”

The king replied: “I obtained this temporary kingdom by the influence of Rama Ekadashi, which falls during the waning moon in the month of October/November. O best of brahmanas, please advise me how I can secure this kingdom permanently. I think the reason the kingdom is temporary is that I observed Ekadashi without faith. Please explain this to Chandrabhaga, the beautiful daughter of King Muchukunda. I think she is capable of making my rule over this kingdom permanent.”

After hearing these words of King Shobhana, the brahmana returned to Muchukundapura and told Chandrabhaga everything in detail. The queen was filled with indescribable joy and said to the brahmana: “O great brahmana! Hearing you, I feel as though I am dreaming a beautiful dream.” The brahmana Somasharma replied to her: “My daughter! With my own eyes I saw your husband in Devapura. I also saw his entire kingdom, radiant like the sun, but he told me that his rule over the kingdom is temporary. Therefore, by every means you must make his rule permanent.”

Chandrabhaga said: “O respected brahmana, please take me there, for my desire to see my husband is great. By the power of my piety I shall make his rule firm. O twice-born one! Please help me, for one who helps those who are separated to reunite acquires merit.”

Then Somasharma took Chandrabhaga to the ashrama of Bamadeva, which was situated near Mount Mandara. After hearing the whole story from radiant-faced Chandrabhaga, Bamadeva initiated her into Vedic mantras.

By the influence of the mantras received from the sage Bamadeva and the piety accumulated through observing Ekadashi, Chandrabhaga obtained a spiritual body. Thereafter Chandrabhaga appeared before her husband. Seeing his wife, Shobhana became extraordinarily joyful and deeply satisfied. Chandrabhaga said: “O my respected husband, please hear my words, which bring auspiciousness. Beginning from the age of eight, I strictly observed Ekadashi in my father’s house. May the piety I have accumulated make your rule stable, and may your sovereignty flourish until the final annihilation of the universe.”

Then, in her divine body, gracefully adorned, she began to enjoy the company of her husband. By the influence of Rama Ekadashi, Shobhana also obtained a divine body and began to enjoy the company of his wife on the summit of Mount Mandara.

Therefore, O king! This Rama Ekadashi is like a wish-fulfilling cow or a philosopher’s stone.”

Lord Krishna continued: “O king! I have told you the glories of this auspicious Rama Ekadashi. A person who strictly observes the vow of this Ekadashi is undoubtedly freed from the sin of killing a brahmana. Just as both white and black cows give white milk, so Ekadashis of both the waxing and waning moons bestow liberation upon their followers. Anyone who hears the glories of this Ekadashi becomes free from the reactions to all sins and happily resides in the abode of Lord Vishnu.”

ekadashi.name: Prabodhini Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Frees one from repeated birth and death and grants devotional service.
ekadashi.story: The day of Lord Vishnu’s awakening from His four-month rest and the conclusion of Chaturmasya.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, November 20, 2026

The glories of Utthana Ekadashi are described in the Skanda Purana in a conversation between Lord Brahma and Narada Muni.

Once Lord Brahma said to Narada Muni: “O best of sages! Please hear from me the glories of Utthana Ekadashi, which destroys the reactions to all sinful activities, increases piety, and bestows liberation. O best of brahmanas! The supreme position of the Ganges remained inferior until Utthana Ekadashi manifested in this world. This Ekadashi falls during the waxing moon in the month of October/November and burns all sins to ashes. The pious influence of oceans and lakes was incomparable only until Utthana, or Haribodhini, Ekadashi appeared. The result attained by performing one thousand horse sacrifices and one hundred Rajasuya sacrifices can easily be attained by observing this Ekadashi.”

Hearing these words of Lord Brahma, Narada Muni said: “O dear father! Please tell me what merit can be obtained by eating once during the day, by eating only supper in the evening, and by fasting completely.”

Lord Brahma replied: “If a person eats once during the day, the reactions to the sinful activities of one lifetime are destroyed. If he eats only supper, the reactions to the sinful activities of two lifetimes are destroyed, and if he fasts completely, the reactions to the sinful activities of seven lifetimes are destroyed. O dear son! This Utthana Ekadashi bestows everything that is unseen, not sought after, and rarely found in the three worlds. This Ekadashi burns to ashes sins as great as Mount Mandara. O lion among sages! If a person acquires any merit on this Ekadashi day, then he obtains results equal to Mount Sumeru. Religious principles cannot dwell in the bodies of people who do not pray to the Lord, who do not follow their vows, who have no faith in God, who revile the Vedas, who blaspheme the sacred scriptures, who enjoy the wives of others, and who are devoid of intelligence.

A person should not commit sins; rather, he should perform pious activities. If a person is inclined toward pious activities, then his religious principles are not destroyed. If a person resolutely follows the vow of Utthana Ekadashi, the reactions to sins committed over one hundred lifetimes are destroyed. If a person remains awake on the night of Utthana Ekadashi, then his ancestors, his relatives in the present life, and his descendants in the future all return to the abode of Vishnu.

O Narada! A person who does not observe the Ekadashi vow in the month of Kartika and does not worship Lord Vishnu loses all the piety he has accumulated. O best of brahmanas! Therefore one should certainly pray to Lord Vishnu in the month of Kartika. If, in the month of Kartika, a person eats food that he prepares for himself, he obtains the results of observing the Chandrayana vrata. If, in the month of Kartika, a person hears narrations about Lord Vishnu and glorifies Him, he obtains the results attained by giving one hundred cows in charity.

By regularly studying the scriptures, a person obtains the results of performing one thousand sacrifices. A person who hears about the Lord and then gives dakshina to the speaker according to his means goes to the Lord’s eternal abode.”

Narada Muni said: “O Lord! Kindly tell me the procedure for observing Ekadashi.”

The great father Brahma replied: “O best of the twice-born! One should rise early in the morning during Brahma-muhurta and, after cleansing the mouth and taking a full bath, worship Lord Keshava. Then one should make a vow by reciting this mantra: ‘I shall fast on Ekadashi day and eat only on Dvadashi. O Pundarikaksha! O Achyuta! I surrender myself unto You! Please protect me.’ One should joyfully and devotionally observe the Ekadashi vow and remain awake throughout the night near the deity of Lord Vishnu. While staying awake all night, one should hear about the transcendental qualities of the Lord. Any pious person who follows these instructions attains the supreme goal. On Ekadashi day one should refrain from every manifestation of greed.”

Lord Brahma continued: “If a person worships Lord Janardana by offering Him kadamba flowers, he does not go to the abode of Yamaraja. If a person worships Lord Garudadhvaja, or Lord Vishnu, in the month of Kartika by offering rose flowers, he certainly attains liberation. If a person worships the Lord by offering bakula and ashoka flowers, he becomes free from sorrow for as long as the sun and moon remain in the sky. If a person worships the Lord by offering sami leaves, he avoids the punishment of Yamaraja. If a person worships Lord Vishnu, the controller of the demigods, by offering Him champaka leaves during the rainy season, he does not have to take birth again in the material world. If a person offers yellow ketaki flowers to Lord Vishnu, all the reactions to sinful activities accumulated over millions of lifetimes are destroyed. If a person offers one hundred fragrant red lotus flowers to Lord Jagannatha, he returns to the Lord’s abode known as Shvetadvipa.

O best of brahmanas! One should remain awake on the night of Ekadashi. On Dvadashi day one should worship Lord Vishnu and complete the observance of the vow by feeding brahmanas. If a person worships the spiritual master and gives gifts according to his means, he satisfies the Supreme Lord.”

ekadashi.name: Padmini Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Grants extraordinary spiritual merit and purification and occurs in the additional month.
ekadashi.story: Connected with the sacred Purushottama month, a special time for repentance and prayer.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, May 27, 2026

There is one subtle point in the observance of Padmini Ekadashi. From the perspective of the Vedic lunar calendar, the concept of a so-called “leap year” is different. Such a leap year does not occur once every four years, as in the Western calendar, but once every three years. In that case, one additional lunar month is added—the month of Purushottama.

The Supreme Lord Sri Krishna, in a conversation with His friend Yudhishthira, said: “...O best of kings, one who observes this fast will undoubtedly attain My personal abode. And if you desire the fulfillment of your wishes, then you should do the same.”

Suta Goswami said: “Anyone who devotionally fasts on the Ekadashi of the additional month of a leap year and carefully follows the regulative principles will become renowned and happily return to Godhead. And one who simply hears or reads about this Ekadashi will also receive great benefit and undoubtedly attain the abode of Lord Hari.”

Originally, Pulastya Muni narrated this story of Padmini Ekadashi to the great Vedic sage Narada Muni, and later the Supreme Lord Sri Krishna told it to His best friend, the sinless King Yudhishthira.

Pulastya Muni once happened to rescue Ravana from the prison of Kartaviryarjuna, and upon hearing about this, Narada Muni asked his friend: “O greatest of sages, Ravana defeated all the demigods, including Lord Indra; how, then, was Kartaviryarjuna able to defeat Ravana, who was so expert in battle?”

Pulastya Muni replied: “O great Narada, in Treta-yuga, Kartavirya, the father of Kartaviryarjuna, took birth in the Haihaya dynasty. His capital was the city of Mahishmati, and he had one thousand queens, each of whom he dearly loved. Yet none of them could give birth to the son he so greatly desired. He performed sacrifices and worshiped the demigods and forefathers, but because of the curse of certain sages he was unable to beget a son. Without a son, the king took no joy in his kingdom, just as a hungry man can never truly enjoy his senses.

King Kartavirya carefully considered his situation and decided to perform severe austerities in order to achieve his goal. Entrusting the rule of the kingdom to his ministers, he put on a bark loincloth, allowed his hair to grow, and went to the forest.

One of his queens, named Padmini—the daughter of King Harishchandra, born in the Ikshvaku dynasty—saw the king leaving. Because she was a chaste woman, she felt it was her duty to follow in the footsteps of her beloved husband. Removing all royal ornaments from her beautiful body and putting on a simple cloth, she followed her husband into the forest.

Eventually Kartavirya reached the summit of Mount Gandhamadana, where he subjected himself to severe austerities for ten thousand years, meditating upon and praying to Lord Gadadhara, the wielder of the club. Nevertheless, he still did not obtain a son. Seeing her dear husband reduced to skin and bones, Padmini found a solution to the problem. She approached the goddess Anasuya, wife of the great sage Atri and mother of Dattatreya, the three-headed incarnation of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva.

Padmini told her about the severe austerities that her dear husband, Kartavirya, had been fruitlessly performing for the past ten thousand years, because Lord Keshava, the only one who could destroy all previous sins and present difficulties, had still not shown him mercy. Then, with the greatest respect, she made this request: “O most fortunate one, please tell me of a fasting day by observing which we can satisfy the Supreme Lord through our devotion and He will grant me a wonderful son who will rule the world as an emperor.”

Hearing the words of Padmini, who was very chaste and devoted to her husband, the great Anasuya replied to her with great encouragement: “O splendid lotus-eyed woman, ordinarily there are twelve months in a year, but after every thirty-two months another month is added, and the two Ekadashis that fall in this month are called Padmini Ekadashi and Parama Ekadashi. They fall on Dvadashi in the bright and dark halves of the month of Purushottama respectively. You should fast on these days and remain awake throughout the night. If you do so, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari, will grant you a son.”

O Narada, in this way Anasuya, the daughter of the sage Kardama, explained the power of these Ekadashis. Having heard her, Padmini faithfully followed the prescribed rules in order to obtain a son. Padmini fasted without even drinking water and remained awake throughout the night, singing the glories of the Lord and dancing in ecstasy. Lord Keshava was very pleased with her devotion and appeared before her, seated upon the back of mighty Garuda. The Lord said: “O beautiful one, you have given Me great pleasure by fasting on the Ekadashi of the additional month of Purushottama. Please ask Me for a blessing.”

Hearing these great words from the Lord of the entire universe, Padmini offered devotional prayers to the Supreme Lord and asked Him to fulfill her husband’s cherished desire. Lord Sri Krishna departed, saying: “O gentle woman, I am very pleased with you and happy, for there is no month dearer to Me than this one, and the Ekadashis that fall in this month are especially dear to Me. You followed Anasuya’s instructions perfectly, and therefore I shall do everything to please you. You and your husband will obtain the son you desire.”

Then the Lord, who frees the world from sorrow, appeared before King Kartavirya: “O king, because your dear and chaste wife has given Me immense pleasure, ask Me for any cherished desire of your heart, and I shall fulfill it.”

The king was extraordinarily happy to hear this. Naturally, he asked for the son he had desired for so long: “O Lord of the universe, O killer of the demon Madhu, mercifully grant me a son who will never be killed by demigods, humans, snakes, demons, or spirits, and whom only You will be able to defeat.” The Supreme Lord immediately said, “So be it!” and departed.

The king was very pleased with his wife and returned with her to the palace. Padmini soon became pregnant, and a son, the mighty-armed Kartaviryarjuna, was born. He was the strongest in all three worlds, and therefore even ten-headed Ravana could not defeat him in battle. Apart from Lord Narayana, who holds the disc, club, and other symbols in His hands, no one could defeat him. He possessed these qualities because his mother had observed Ekadashi very strictly and with faith, and therefore he was able to defeat the terrible Ravana. This is not astonishing, O Naradaji, because Kartaviryarjuna was a blessing of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.”

The Supreme Lord Sri Krishna concluded: “O sinless Yudhishthira, because you asked Me, I have explained to you the power of this special Ekadashi. O best of kings, one who observes this fast will undoubtedly attain My personal abode. And if you desire the fulfillment of your wishes, you should do the same.”

Thus ends the narration from the Skanda Purana concerning the glories of Padmini Ekadashi, the Ekadashi of the bright half of the additional month in a leap year.

ekadashi.name: Parama Ekadashi
ekadashi.benefits: Destroys poverty and sins, grants all auspiciousness, and elevates consciousness.
ekadashi.story: A great fast of Purushottama month that removes the consequences of unrighteous acts.
ekadashi.full_description:
Ekadashi, June 11, 2026

Yudhishthira Maharaja said: “O Supreme Lord, what is the name of the Ekadashi that falls during the dark half of the additional month of a leap year? O Lord of all universes, how should it properly be observed? Kindly tell me this.”

The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Sri Krishna, replied: “O Yudhishthira, this praiseworthy day is called Parama Ekadashi. It bestows the great blessing of a joyful life and final liberation from birth and death. Observing it is like observing the Ekadashi of the bright half of the month of Kartika. On this Ekadashi one should worship Me, the best of all living beings, with great love and devotion. In this connection, I shall now tell you a beautiful story exactly as I heard it from the great sages in the city of Kampilya.

Once, in Kampilya, there lived a pious brahmana named Sumedha with his wife Pavitra, who was very chaste and devoted to her husband. Because of sins accumulated in a previous life, Sumedha had neither money nor grain, and even though he begged many people for food, he lived in hunger. He could scarcely feed, clothe, and shelter himself and his beautiful young wife, who had such an excellent character that she continued faithfully serving Sumedha despite his poverty. Whenever guests came to their home, Pavitra always gave them food, although she herself was often hungry; her beautiful lotus-like face never became gloomy. Hunger made her weak, but her service to Sumedha remained unbroken.

Seeing all this and lamenting his unfortunate fate, Sumedha one day said to Pavitra: “My dear wife, O most beautiful one, I beg alms from wealthy people and receive only remnants. What am I to do? How can our situation be changed? Where should I seek help? O most obedient and loving wife, without sufficient prosperity the affairs of a householder can never be successful. Therefore allow me to go to foreign lands and obtain wealth. If I make such an effort, I shall certainly obtain the fortune necessary for happiness. Without effort, a person cannot fulfill his desires and needs. The wise say that an effort undertaken with enthusiasm is always auspicious.”

Hearing these words from her husband, Pavitra folded her palms, her eyes filled with tears, and she said to him with the greatest respect and love: “I think there is no greater and more learned person than you, my dear. One who thinks of the welfare of others even in distress speaks as you do now.

However, the sacred scriptures say that the wealth a person possesses in this life depends upon pious activities performed in previous lives; and if he did not give charity in previous lives, then even while sitting upon a mountain of gold equal to Mount Sumeru, he may remain a pauper. Any charity in the form of education, money, fertile land, and so forth will return to him in future lives. We receive what we give. No one will obtain any prosperity if he did not give charity in a previous life. O best of brahmanas, since we are now poor, it means that in our previous life neither you nor I gave charity to the poor. Therefore, O merciful husband, you should remain here with me. Without you I cannot live even for a moment.

Without her husband, a woman will not be welcomed by her father, mother, brother, father-in-law, or any other family member. Everyone will say, ‘You have lost your husband, unfortunate woman!’ Therefore I shall be severely condemned. Please remain with me and be satisfied with what we have. What is destined for us, we shall obtain properly in due time, and we shall enjoy complete happiness here.”

Having heard these plaintive words of his wife, Sumedha decided to remain in his native village. One day the great sage Kaundinya arrived there, and upon seeing him, the brahmana Sumedha and his wife came before him and offered their humble respects. With bowed head, Sumedha welcomed him: “We are very happy to welcome you here today, O wisest of sages. My life has become happy, and I am greatly indebted to you.” Sumedha offered Kaundinya Muni a comfortable seat and highly praised his austerity and learning.

“By receiving your darshan today,” Sumedha said, “I have become very fortunate.” The poor brahmana couple fed the sage as abundantly and exquisitely as they could, after which Pavitra asked him: “O most learned one, what must we do to become free from poverty? How can a person who gave no charity in a previous life obtain a good family, prosperity, and excellent education? My husband wishes to leave me and go to foreign lands to beg alms, but I implore him to remain with me. I humbly told him that if someone lacks prosperity in this life, it is because he did not adequately give charity in previous lives. Therefore he decided to remain here. It is my great good fortune that you have mercifully appeared today. Surely we shall now soon see the end of our poverty.

O best of brahmanas, please tell us how we can become free from these constant sufferings caused by poverty. O merciful one, kindly describe to us a remedy—whether a place of pilgrimage we should visit, a day on which we should fast, or an austerity we should perform—by which our misfortune may disappear forever.”

Hearing this sincere plea from the patient woman, the great sage Kaundinya remained silent for some time and then said: “There is a fasting day that is very dear to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Hari. Fasting on this day destroys all sins and carries away all the suffering caused by poverty. This fasting day, which occurs during the dark half of the additional month of a leap year, is known as Parama Ekadashi. It is the supreme day of Lord Vishnu. This Ekadashi bestows everything necessary in life—money, grain—and ultimately grants liberation. When evening comes on this day, one should begin singing the glories of the Lord and dancing in ecstasy, and continue throughout the night.

Lord Kuvera once observed this sacred day with great faith. Lord Shiva, seeing how carefully he fasted, became very pleased and made Kuvera the treasurer of heaven. King Harishchandra also fasted on this Ekadashi at a time when his wife and son had been sold, and by doing so he was able to regain them. Thereafter he ruled the kingdom without obstruction. Therefore, O wide-eyed woman, you should always observe the sacred fast of Parama Ekadashi, following all the relevant rules and regulations and remaining awake throughout the night.”

Then he said to Sumedha: “On Dvadashi, the day after Ekadashi, you should observe the Pancharatrika fast according to the rules and regulations. After bathing early in the morning, you and your wife, together with your parents and hers, should fast for five days according to your ability. Then you will become worthy of returning home, to the abode of Lord Vishnu.

A person who does this even once will go to the heavenly planets. One who properly feeds a worthy brahmana during these five days receives the result of having fed all the demigods, human beings, and even demons. One who gives a jug of water in charity to a twice-born brahmana during these five days of fasting obtains benefit equal to the reward for giving the entire earthly planet in charity. Anyone who gives a learned person a pot filled with sesame seeds will live in heaven for as many years as there are seeds in the pot. One who gives a pot filled with golden ghee will certainly go to the abode of the sun-god after fully enjoying life on this earth. One who abstains from sexual relations during these five days will attain heavenly happiness and enjoy with the maidens of Indraloka.

Therefore both of you—you, Sumedha, and you, Pavitra—should fast during these five days of Pancharatrika in order to receive the reward of abundant grain and wealth for the remainder of your lives on this planet. After this world, the spiritual realm will be your dwelling place.”

Having heard this great advice, the brahmana couple Sumedha and Pavitra properly observed the Pancharatrika fast on Parama Ekadashi and soon saw a beautiful prince who had come to them from the royal palace. By the order of Lord Brahma, the prince gave them a wonderful, exquisitely furnished house and invited them to live in it. Praising their austerity and patience, he gave them an entire village for their livelihood and then returned to the palace. Thus Sumedha and his wife enjoyed all the blessings of this world and later went to the abode of Vishnu.

Anyone who observes the fast of Parama Ekadashi as well as the Pancharatrika fast becomes free from all sins and, after enjoying life here, returns to Vishnuloka, just like the brahmana Sumedha and his devoted wife Pavitra. O Yudhishthira, it is impossible to calculate the benefit obtained by fasting on Parama Ekadashi, for observing it is equal to bathing at holy places such as Lake Pushkara and the Ganges, giving cows in charity, and performing all other religious activities. One who fasts on this day has already made offerings to the forefathers at Gaya. He obtains the same reward as from fasting on all other auspicious days.

Just as the brahminical varna is considered the best among the varnas, just as the cow is the best among four-legged animals, and just as Lord Indra is the best of the demigods, so the additional month of a leap year is the best among months.

It is said that the Pancharatrika fast, the five-day fast of the additional month, removes all kinds of abominable sins. But the Pancharatrika fast, together with fasting on Parama Ekadashi and Padmini Ekadashi, destroys all of a person’s sins. If someone cannot fast on all these days, he should observe fasting during the additional month according to his ability. One who has received a human birth but does not properly bathe during the additional month and does not observe this Ekadashi, which is very dear to Lord Hari, commits suicide and will suffer by taking birth among the 8,400,000 species of living beings.

The rare human life is meant for attaining blessing and subsequent liberation. Therefore one should in every way observe the fast on this auspicious Parama Ekadashi.

Lord Krishna concluded: “O sinless Yudhishthira, according to your request I have described to you the great benefit obtained by fasting on the Ekadashi called Parama, which falls during the two dark weeks of the additional month of a leap year. If possible, you should observe this fast.”

King Yudhishthira acted exactly according to the instructions of Lord Krishna, and so did all his brothers and their wife Draupadi. After enjoying rare bliss in the material world, they returned home, back to Godhead. Anyone who properly performs the prescribed bathing and fasts on these two Ekadashis of the additional month will go to heaven and ultimately attain the abode of Sri Vishnu, and when he goes there, all the demigods will praise him and offer prayers to him.”

Thus ends the narration from the Skanda Purana concerning the glories of Parama Ekadashi, the Ekadashi of the two dark weeks of the additional month of a leap year.
